headline: Musadik seeks climate-resilient development
description: Musadik seeks climate-resilient development
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

Minister for Climate Change Musadik Malik on Monday called for a shift towards rights-based and climate-resilient development.

He stressed that poor and vulnerable communities should not continue to bear the disproportionate burden of climate change, global economic inequalities and mounting debt.

Addressing the inaugural plenary session of the 29th Sustainable Development Conference (SDC 2026) under the theme "Rethinking Development in an Age of Disruption," the minister said development should not be measured merely in dollars but by its impact on the lives and future generations of ordinary people.

headline: Court upholds warrants against CM Afridi
description: Court upholds warrants against CM Afridi
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

ISLAMABAD. The District and Sessions Court of Islamabad on Monday upheld non-bailable arrest warrants against Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi over his repeated absence from court proceedings in a case involving allegations against state institutions.

The court has ordered his arrest and directed authorities to produce him before the court.

Judicial Magistrate Malik Aman heard the case registered against Afridi under the PECA.

The court maintained the non-bailable arrest warrants issued against him due to his failure to appear before the court.

The court adjourned further hearing until Nov 15.

headline: PM warns banks over slow loans
description: PM warns banks over slow loans
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The prime minister directed the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and the Ministry of Finance on Monday not to extend concessions to banks failing to expedite lending to farmers, small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and consumers under the Apna Ghar housing scheme.

He was chairing a review meeting on facilitation of credit provision to priority sectors.

"Banks that are performing well in facilitating credit provision to agriculture, housing and small and medium enterprises under government initiatives are commendable," the premier said.

"The State Bank and the Ministry of Finance should not give concessions to banks that are slow in providing loans to farmers, small and medium enterprises and consumers under the Prime Minister's Apna Ghar scheme, a part of government initiatives," he added.

The prime minister emphasised that improvement in the economy and employment provision to youth through development of small and medium enterprises, housing and agriculture sectors was the top priority of the government.

"Banks are of key importance for the development of the private sector. Banks should extend cooperation in providing loans to priority sectors in the same way as the government and its agencies cooperate with banks," he said.

"Small and medium enterprises have great potential to grow the economy, promote exports and create employment opportunities. The agriculture sector is the backbone of the country's economy and efforts are being made to increase exports through value addition of agricultural commodities," he added.

"Apna Ghar scheme will promote many industries related to the housing and construction sector."

The premier directed the finance minister to resolve issues related to financing of stakeholders of the SME sector, agriculture and housing sectors and formulate a comprehensive action plan.

He also directed the SBP and the Federal Board of Revenue to jointly resolve tax issues of small and medium enterprises and exporters and formulate a comprehensive risk coverage strategy for easy provision of loans to small and medium enterprises.

The participants of the meeting were informed that the SBP was working on three basic pillars to increase the provision of loans to priority sectors, which include improving regulations, sharing of risks and costs between the government and banks, and promotion of digital facilities.

Jinnah Medical Complex

The prime minister termed the ongoing construction work on Jinnah Medical Complex (JMC) as satisfactory and stressed that targets must be achieved within the stipulated timeframe.

He also directed the authorities concerned that all appointments in the facility should be made purely on merit and in a transparent manner.

The premier expressed these views while chairing a high-level meeting to assess the progress on the under-construction JMC, a state-of-the-art healthcare facility being built to international standards, PM Office Media Wing said in a press release.

ISLAMABAD:

The prime minister directed the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and the Ministry of Finance on Monday not to extend concessions to banks failing to expedite lending to farmers, small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and consumers under the Apna Ghar housing scheme.

He was chairing a review meeting on facilitation of credit provision to priority sectors.

"Banks that are performing well in facilitating credit provision to agriculture, housing and small and medium enterprises under government initiatives are commendable," the premier said.

"The State Bank and the Ministry of Finance should not give concessions to banks that are slow in providing loans to farmers, small and medium enterprises and consumers under the Prime Minister's Apna Ghar scheme, a part of government initiatives," he added.

The prime minister emphasised that improvement in the economy and employment provision to youth through development of small and medium enterprises, housing and agriculture sectors was the top priority of the government.

"Banks are of key importance for the development of the private sector. Banks should extend cooperation in providing loans to priority sectors in the same way as the government and its agencies cooperate with banks," he said.

"Small and medium enterprises have great potential to grow the economy, promote exports and create employment opportunities. The agriculture sector is the backbone of the country's economy and efforts are being made to increase exports through value addition of agricultural commodities," he added.

"Apna Ghar scheme will promote many industries related to the housing and construction sector."

The premier directed the finance minister to resolve issues related to financing of stakeholders of the SME sector, agriculture and housing sectors and formulate a comprehensive action plan.

He also directed the SBP and the Federal Board of Revenue to jointly resolve tax issues of small and medium enterprises and exporters and formulate a comprehensive risk coverage strategy for easy provision of loans to small and medium enterprises.

The participants of the meeting were informed that the SBP was working on three basic pillars to increase the provision of loans to priority sectors, which include improving regulations, sharing of risks and costs between the government and banks, and promotion of digital facilities.

Jinnah Medical Complex

The prime minister termed the ongoing construction work on Jinnah Medical Complex (JMC) as satisfactory and stressed that targets must be achieved within the stipulated timeframe.

He also directed the authorities concerned that all appointments in the facility should be made purely on merit and in a transparent manner.

The premier expressed these views while chairing a high-level meeting to assess the progress on the under-construction JMC, a state-of-the-art healthcare facility being built to international standards, PM Office Media Wing said in a press release.

headline: Fazl criticises govt's approach to ex-FATA
description: Fazl criticises govt's approach to ex-FATA
author: Wisal Yousafzai
article_text:
JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman has said the former tribal districts have long been treated as experimental grounds, adding that there is an ongoing debate in the power corridors to reverse their merger with Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P).

Speaking to the media on Monday, Fazl said nearly a decade had passed since the merger of the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas (Fata) with K-P, but the promised administrative and governance arrangements had yet to be put in place.

He claimed that he had been told at a high level that the mergerwhich took place in 2018 during the PML-N's rulewas a mistake, questioning who had originally approved the decision and who was now pushing proposals to reverse it.

"The issue today is not constitutional; it is about the resources of the tribal areas," he said, adding that he had repeatedly raised concerns about mineral reserves in the region even before the imposition of governor's rule and emergency measures last month.

Fazl said his party had no objection to the exploration and development of mineral resources but insisted that all agreements concerning the region's natural wealth should be made public.

He further claimed that the United States was showing a growing interest in the region's precious stones, alleging that gemstones had been presented at American offices and that US officials had acknowledged the development.

He also criticised the government's handling of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), saying China had been disappointed while, according to him, the United States was now taking its place.

Questioning the rationale behind the imposition of governor's rule and emergency measures in parts of K-P, the JUI-F chief said these decisions had been justified on the grounds of terrorism, but the narrative surrounding terrorism had subsided after the measures were introduced on October 11.

headline: 'Medical treatment: gross negligence can be penalised'
description: 'Medical treatment: gross negligence can be penalised'
author: Hasnaat Malik
article_text:
The Supreme Court has held that a doctor cannot be held criminally liable merely because a patient suffers an injury or dies during treatment, unless the prosecution establishes gross negligence warranting penal consequences.

In a six-page judgment authored by Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim, the court explained the distinction between ordinary professional negligence and criminally culpable conduct while dismissing an appeal against the acquittal of doctors accused of medical negligence.

It held that criminal liability requires proof of a duty of care, a breach of that duty resulting in death, and gross negligence on the part of the medical professional.

"We would like to elaborate on the concept of negligence and how such negligence is to be treated in case of medical professionals. Negligence is either the omission to do something which a reasonable and prudent person would ordinarily do in the circumstances, or the commission of an act which such a person would refrain from doing," the ruling stated.

The case arose from the death of the petitioner's wife, who was taken to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad after experiencing labour pain and underwent a procedure in the labour room, where she delivered twin girls.

The petitioner alleged that the doctors had administered spinal anaesthesia instead of an epidural injection, contrary to his request.

He maintained that his wife subsequently developed back pain, which worsened over time and eventually led to her death. The complaint was dismissed, and the Islamabad High Court later upheld the doctors' acquittal.

Hearing an appeal against the IHC ruling, a Supreme Court division bench headed by Justice Muhammad Hashim Kakar observed that negligence could attract legal liability only if three essential elements were established: a duty of care, a breach of that duty and damage resulting from the breach.

"We are of the view that for prosecution to establish that a death occurred due to medical negligence under provisions of section 319 Qatl-i-Khata by rash and negligent act the prosecution must prove (i) the existence of duty; (ii) a breach of the duty causing death and (iii) the breach of the duty must be characterised as gross negligence by that medical professional. The mere fact that injury or death has occurred during medical treatment cannot, in itself, substitute for proof of this heightened degree of negligence," the judgment said.

The court observed that the existence of an error or an undesirable outcome, by itself, did not establish negligence, as the alleged commission or omission must be connected with the injury sustained.

The judgment noted that a mere error of judgment, an accident or a simple lapse in care did not, without more, establish professional negligence.

"A medical practitioner cannot be held liable merely because another course of treatment was available or a more experienced practitioner might have adopted a different approach."

The court said the relevant question was whether the practitioner had acted in accordance with a practice accepted as proper by the medical profession at the time and exercised the degree of care and competence reasonably expected under the circumstances.

"Nor can liability be founded merely upon the failure to adopt extraordinary precautions simply because, in hindsight, they might have prevented the eventual harm."

"A medical professional may be found negligent where the requisite professional skill is lacking or where the skill possessed is not exercised with reasonable competence in the particular case.

"The applicable standard is that of an ordinarily competent practitioner exercising ordinary professional skill in the relevant field, rather than that of the most highly skilled or exceptionally experienced specialist."

The judgment said the law did not demand perfection from a medical practitioner, but only required the exercise of reasonable professional competence in discharging the duty owed to a patient.

Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim further observed that it was equally important to distinguish negligence actionable under civil law from negligence attracting criminal liability.

"Conduct sufficient to establish civil negligence does not necessarily constitute a criminal offence as in numerous situations a case for civil liability will be made but criminal liability will not be made out."

The judgment said criminal liability required a substantially higher degree of negligence, characterised by grossness or a degree of recklessness serious enough to warrant penal consequences.

The petitioner alleged that the doctors had administered spinal anaesthesia instead of an epidural injection, contrary to his request.

He maintained that his wife subsequently developed back pain, which worsened over time and eventually led to her death. The complaint was dismissed, and the Islamabad High Court later upheld the doctors' acquittal.

Hearing an appeal against the IHC ruling, a Supreme Court division bench headed by Justice Muhammad Hashim Kakar observed that negligence could attract legal liability only if three essential elements were established: a duty of care, a breach of that duty and damage resulting from the breach.

"We are of the view that for prosecution to establish that a death occurred due to medical negligence under provisions of section 319 Qatl-i-Khata by rash and negligent act the prosecution must prove (i) the existence of duty; (ii) a breach of the duty causing death and (iii) the breach of the duty must be characterised as gross negligence by that medical professional. The mere fact that injury or death has occurred during medical treatment cannot, in itself, substitute for proof of this heightened degree of negligence," the judgment said.

The court observed that the existence of an error or an undesirable outcome, by itself, did not establish negligence, as the alleged commission or omission must be connected with the injury sustained.

The judgment noted that a mere error of judgment, an accident or a simple lapse in care did not, without more, establish professional negligence.

"A medical practitioner cannot be held liable merely because another course of treatment was available or a more experienced practitioner might have adopted a different approach."

The court said the relevant question was whether the practitioner had acted in accordance with a practice accepted as proper by the medical profession at the time and exercised the degree of care and competence reasonably expected under the circumstances.

"Nor can liability be founded merely upon the failure to adopt extraordinary precautions simply because, in hindsight, they might have prevented the eventual harm."

"A medical professional may be found negligent where the requisite professional skill is lacking or where the skill possessed is not exercised with reasonable competence in the particular case.

"The applicable standard is that of an ordinarily competent practitioner exercising ordinary professional skill in the relevant field, rather than that of the most highly skilled or exceptionally experienced specialist."

The judgment said the law did not demand perfection from a medical practitioner, but only required the exercise of reasonable professional competence in discharging the duty owed to a patient.

Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim further observed that it was equally important to distinguish negligence actionable under civil law from negligence attracting criminal liability.

"Conduct sufficient to establish civil negligence does not necessarily constitute a criminal offence as in numerous situations a case for civil liability will be made but criminal liability will not be made out."

The judgment said criminal liability required a substantially higher degree of negligence, characterised by grossness or a degree of recklessness serious enough to warrant penal consequences.

headline: ECP reviews Islamabad LG poll preparations
description: CEC chaired a meeting to review preparations for the Islamabad local government elections
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
CEC chaired a meeting to review preparations for the Islamabad local government elections

Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Sikandar Sultan Raja on Monday expressed satisfaction over preparations for the upcoming local government (LG) elections in Islamabad and directed the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) to convene a meeting on Nov 10 to review arrangements and assess the security plan.

The meeting will be attended by the interior secretary, Islamabad chief commissioner and Islamabad IGP, who will brief the commission on security arrangements and other election-related matters.

According to a statement issued by the ECP spokesperson, the CEC chaired a meeting to review preparations for the Islamabad local government elections, during which the ECP secretary and other senior officials briefed him on the electoral process.

The briefing covered the Islamabad local government system, election procedures for various seats, arrangements made so far and the future course of action. The CEC was informed that the procurement of all election-related materials had been completed and arrangements for printing ballot papers were also in place.

The commission has also written to the interior secretary, Islamabad IGP and deputy commissioner, requesting necessary arrangements for the smooth conduct of the elections.

headline: Two killed in separate incidents
description: Two killed in separate incidents
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Two men were reportedly shot dead in separate incidents of murder in Rawalpindi.

According to the police, a man named Ajmal, who resides in Peshawar, filed a complaint in which he stated that his brother, Adnan, lived in Chakra along with their mother and brother-in-law, Atta. He said that Adnan used to work as a driver for a cigarette company.

Ajmal said that on the day of the incident, he received a call from his brother-in-law, who told him that Adnan had been murdered by an unidentified armed individual who broke into their house and shot him.

In a separate incident, a tikka shop owner was shot dead following a dispute that took place after someone parked their rickshaw in front of his shop, in Scheme III, Ghareebabad, in the jurisdiction of the Chaklala Police Station.

According to the police, the victim, a hardworking man named Sain Hafeez, was busy working at his tikka shop when a rickshaw driver named Shahid parked his vehicle in front of the premises. When Hafeez objected, an argument ensued, prompting the rickshaw driver to pull a pistol from his vehicle and open fire.

headline: Millers threaten strike over police action
description: Millers threaten strike over police action
author: Qaiser Shirazi
article_text:
The Pakistan Flour Mills Association has announced a complete strike if cases are not registered against the police personnel responsible for allegedly assaulting the owner of a Taxila flour mill and the FIR registered against him is not withdrawn within 48 hours.

The association has warned that it will first suspend flour supplies across the Rawalpindi Division, followed by a complete halt to supplies across Punjab within 72 hours. It has also threatened a nationwide protest if its demands are not met.

The decision was announced at an emergency meeting of the association, chaired by its group leader, Qaid Asim Raza Ahmed, and Patron-in-Chief Tariq Sadiq.

Participants were informed that police Security Branch personnel allegedly misbehaved with and assaulted Sheikh Abu Bakar, owner of Lasani Flour Mills in Taxila. Instead of taking action against the officials concerned, police registered a case against the mill owner and subsequently sealed the flour mill by force, allegedly to harass him.

The association condemned the incident, terming it an act of hooliganism and misuse of authority. It demanded that cases be registered against Security Branch personnel Zaheer and Zamin Shah for allegedly abusing their powers and assaulting the mill owner.

The association said it supported the Punjab government's policies and that flour mill owners were responsible businesspeople who paid substantial taxes. However, it would not tolerate police high-handedness, which, it said, was making it increasingly difficult for businesses to operate.

The association also demanded immediate legal action against the Food Department officials and police Security Branch personnel allegedly involved in the incident.

It warned that failure to register cases against those responsible and withdraw the FIR against the mill owner within two days would result in a complete suspension of flour supplies across the Rawalpindi Division. Supplies across Punjab would be halted on the third day, followed by a nationwide protest.

The association urged Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz to take immediate notice of the incident, alleging that the police and Food Department were undermining the provincial government's policies.

Subsidised flour shortage

The closure of one of the two major depots supplying subsidised flour to tandoors for the sale of roti at Rs20 has severely affected the cheap roti scheme across the district.

Only around 150 out of 7,000 tandoors are reportedly receiving subsidised flour at the official rate from the remaining depot, triggering a crisis in the supply system.

The sale of subsidised red-flour roti at 90 per cent of tandoors is suspended after sunset because of flour shortages. The Naanbai Association has announced that it will not purchase expensive flour from the open market and sell roti at the subsidised price of Rs20 if cheap flour is not provided.

Association Central President Shafiq Abbasi said tandoors in Rawalpindi district were supplied a 20kg bag of subsidised flour for Rs2,200 to sell roti at Rs20. Large tandoors previously received up to 10 bags daily, while small neighbourhood tandoors were supplied up to five bags. Two major depots had been established to ensure supplies.

CRAWLEY, UK/ RAWALPINDI:

The Pakistan Flour Mills Association has announced a complete strike if cases are not registered against the police personnel responsible for allegedly assaulting the owner of a Taxila flour mill and the FIR registered against him is not withdrawn within 48 hours.

The association has warned that it will first suspend flour supplies across the Rawalpindi Division, followed by a complete halt to supplies across Punjab within 72 hours. It has also threatened a nationwide protest if its demands are not met.

The decision was announced at an emergency meeting of the association, chaired by its group leader, Qaid Asim Raza Ahmed, and Patron-in-Chief Tariq Sadiq.

Participants were informed that police Security Branch personnel allegedly misbehaved with and assaulted Sheikh Abu Bakar, owner of Lasani Flour Mills in Taxila. Instead of taking action against the officials concerned, police registered a case against the mill owner and subsequently sealed the flour mill by force, allegedly to harass him.

The association condemned the incident, terming it an act of hooliganism and misuse of authority. It demanded that cases be registered against Security Branch personnel Zaheer and Zamin Shah for allegedly abusing their powers and assaulting the mill owner.

The association said it supported the Punjab government's policies and that flour mill owners were responsible businesspeople who paid substantial taxes. However, it would not tolerate police high-handedness, which, it said, was making it increasingly difficult for businesses to operate.

The association also demanded immediate legal action against the Food Department officials and police Security Branch personnel allegedly involved in the incident.

It warned that failure to register cases against those responsible and withdraw the FIR against the mill owner within two days would result in a complete suspension of flour supplies across the Rawalpindi Division. Supplies across Punjab would be halted on the third day, followed by a nationwide protest.

The association urged Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz to take immediate notice of the incident, alleging that the police and Food Department were undermining the provincial government's policies.

Subsidised flour shortage

The closure of one of the two major depots supplying subsidised flour to tandoors for the sale of roti at Rs20 has severely affected the cheap roti scheme across the district.

Only around 150 out of 7,000 tandoors are reportedly receiving subsidised flour at the official rate from the remaining depot, triggering a crisis in the supply system.

The sale of subsidised red-flour roti at 90 per cent of tandoors is suspended after sunset because of flour shortages. The Naanbai Association has announced that it will not purchase expensive flour from the open market and sell roti at the subsidised price of Rs20 if cheap flour is not provided.

Association Central President Shafiq Abbasi said tandoors in Rawalpindi district were supplied a 20kg bag of subsidised flour for Rs2,200 to sell roti at Rs20. Large tandoors previously received up to 10 bags daily, while small neighbourhood tandoors were supplied up to five bags. Two major depots had been established to ensure supplies.

headline: German envoy urges stronger trade ties
description: German envoy urges stronger trade ties
author: Zulfiqar Baig
article_text:
German Ambassador to Pakistan Dr Ina Lepel visited the National Press Club (NPC), Islamabad, and attended a special interactive session with journalists under the club's international outreach initiative, "Meet the Press".

During the visit, the ambassador toured different sections of the National Press Club and later planted a sapling on its premises as a symbol of friendship and environmental sustainability.

She was warmly received by NPC President Abdul Razzaq Sial, Secretary Dr Furqan Rao, members of the governing body and senior journalists.

Welcoming the ambassador, the NPC president expressed hope that such interactions would continue in the future. On the occasion, NPC Secretary Dr Furqan Rao also welcomed her and gave a detailed briefing on the club's history, journalistic activities, institutional role and initiatives for the welfare of journalists.

Dr Furqan Rao said Germany was an important development partner of Pakistan and the two countries had longstanding cooperation in various fields, including trade, education, development projects and strengthening democratic institutions.

He added that Germany was also playing an important role in providing higher education opportunities and scholarships to Pakistani youth.

Addressing the Meet the Press programme, German Ambassador Dr Ina Lepel highlighted the longstanding friendly relations between Pakistan and Germany and stressed the need for a significant increase in bilateral trade.

She pointed out that despite the passage of several years, the volume of trade between the two countries had not increased as desired.

She said she had previously served in Pakistan in 2017 and had now returned as ambassador, but regretted that bilateral trade had not witnessed any substantial improvement during this period.

headline: Weapons, drugs seized at bus stand
description: Weapons, drugs seized at bus stand
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

Disappointed with the alleged poor performance of Pirwadhai police and its failure to take effective action against drug addicts, pickpockets and criminal elements despite repeated complaints, the Regional Transport Authority (RTA), responsible for regulating public transport, took matters into its own hands and conducted a major operation in collaboration with the Civil Defence.

Staff of the transport authority, accompanied by Civil Defence personnel, have conducted a major operation at Pirwadhai General Bus Stand, the city's largest bus terminal, over the past 10 days, seizing a large quantity of knives, cutters, equipment used for drug consumption and other suspicious items.

According to sources, the presence of drug addicts, pickpockets and other suspicious individuals at Pirwadhai General Bus Stand had been brought to the attention of the relevant police authorities on several occasions.

headline: Man convicted of harassing minor
description: Man convicted of harassing minor
author: APP
article_text:
The District and Sessions Court of Islamabad on Monday sentenced a man to seven years of rigorous imprisonment for harassing a 16-year-old boy and recording an inappropriate video without his consent.

The court also imposed a fine of Rs1 million on the convict.

Additional Sessions Judge Muhammad Afzal Majoka announced the verdict in a case registered under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA).

The court found the main accused, Raja Haris Naveed, guilty of the charges and awarded him seven years of rigorous imprisonment.

The court also directed him to pay a fine of Rs1 million. In case of non-payment, he will have to serve an additional six months in prison.

However, the court acquitted co-accused Shahzaib Meraj, giving him the benefit of the doubt after finding that the charge of assisting in the crime had not been established.

According to the case details, the main accused allegedly lured a 16-year-old matriculation student into a drawing room and locked him inside.

He then allegedly used a firearm to threaten and harass the minor before recording an inappropriate video without his consent.

headline: IHC orders recovery of girl
description: IHC orders recovery of girl
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has directed the police to recover a girl who has been missing for nine months and produce her before the court within two weeks.

Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro issued the directive while hearing a petition filed by the missing girl's father, Abid Hussain. The investigation officer (IO) informed the court that positive progress had been made in the case and that efforts were under way to produce the girl before the court soon.

The petitioner's counsel submitted that despite the passage of several months, no significant progress had been made. A joint investigation team (JIT) had been constituted after the family lost confidence in the police, but the girl had still not been recovered. The counsel also pointed out that the geofencing report had yet to be received.

The counsel representing the police informed the court that the JIT's latest meeting had been held on October 20 and that the police were conducting operations in coordination with various agencies.

Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro issued the directive while hearing a petition filed by the missing girl's father, Abid Hussain. The investigation officer (IO) informed the court that positive progress had been made in the case and that efforts were under way to produce the girl before the court soon.

The petitioner's counsel submitted that despite the passage of several months, no significant progress had been made. A joint investigation team (JIT) had been constituted after the family lost confidence in the police, but the girl had still not been recovered. The counsel also pointed out that the geofencing report had yet to be received.

The counsel representing the police informed the court that the JIT's latest meeting had been held on October 20 and that the police were conducting operations in coordination with various agencies.

headline: Punjab approves Rs1.1b for CT scanners
description: Punjab approves Rs1.1b for CT scanners
author: Jamil Mirza
article_text:
The Punjab government has approved Rs1.1 billion for the installation of modern CT scan machines at three major hospitals in the province, including Rawalpindi's Benazir Bhutto General Hospital. Patients at the hospital had been facing difficulties because its existing CT scanner frequently developed faults.

According to the Health Department, the provincial government has approved Rs1.1 billion for the provision of modern CT scanners at three major public-sector hospitals.

An amount of Rs500 million has been allocated for the purchase of a modern whole-body multi-ultrafast CT scanner for cardiac examinations at the Punjab Institute of Cardiology in Lahore.

Similarly, Rs300 million has been approved for installing a 128-slice CT scanner in the emergency department of Lahore General Hospital to replace its old machine.

Another Rs300 million has been sanctioned for purchasing a modern 128-slice CT scanner for Benazir Bhutto Hospital in Rawalpindi.

Administrative approval for all three projects has been granted by Punjab Health Secretary Azmat Mahmood.

Secretary of Specialised Healthcare and Medical Education Azmat Mahmood said that, under the vision of Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif, work was under way on projects worth billions of rupees to provide modern medical and diagnostic facilities to people across the province.

He said the Punjab government remained committed to providing quality healthcare facilities to the people.

Allied hospitals get Rs6.9b

On the other hand, the 20th meeting of the Syndicate of Rawalpindi Medical University (RMU) has approved an annual budget of Rs6.9 billion for the university and its three allied hospitals for the financial year 202627, along with Rs338.7 million for the PLA account and additional funds exceeding Rs688.8m to meet outstanding liabilities from the previous financial year.

The Syndicate approved the revised budget for the previous financial year, the budget for the current financial year and the university's revised budget relating to the Higher Education Commission.

It also approved Rs196.1m for the improvement and rehabilitation of the sewerage system at Holy Family Hospital (HFH). An allocation of Rs29.3m was approved for payments to the National Institute of Health (NIH) for the purchase of vaccines, while Rs38.6m was sanctioned for the settlement of contingency bills.

The meeting further approved the nomination of new Syndicate members to the university's Selection Board, adoption of the Undergraduate Attendance Policy 2027, and nominations to the Board of Advanced Studies and Research.

The meeting was chaired by Punjab Health Minister Khawaja Salman Rafique and attended by RMU Vice-Chancellor Major General (retd) Sohail Amin, Syndicate members Dr Jamal Nasir, General (retd) Aslam and Dr Semi Gul, Syed Tahir Shahbaz, Parliamentary Secretary and Syndicate member Ziaullah Shah, Director Budget and Accounts Hammadur Rehman, Deputy Secretary Medical Education Usama Javed, and the medical superintendents of the university's three allied hospitals.

headline: Intermediate supplementary examinations begin
description: Intermediate supplementary examinations begin
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The Intermediate Second Annual (Supplementary) Examinations organised by the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE) Rawalpindi will begin today.

Roll number slips have been issued to candidates and the necessary staff has been deployed to all examination centres. The Rawalpindi Education Board has established a total of 41 examination centres: 7 in Attock district, 4 in Chakwal district, 2 in Talagang district, 5 in Jhelum district, 2 in Murree district and 17 in Rawalpindi district. This includes 11 centres for male students, 12 for female students and 17 co-educational centres.

All examination centres have been linked to a Command and Control Centre to facilitate online monitoring. Furthermore, surveillance cameras have been installed at all centres to ensure the examination process remains transparent, fair and well-organised.

Additionally, a high-level meeting was held under the chairmanship of Rawalpindi Education Board Chairman Dr Iqbal Mahmood to review the exam preparations. The meeting was attended by Controller of Examinations Mubashir Saeed and Board Secretary Zulkaif Umar Shah. The meeting reviewed the examination arrangements, security, supervision, distribution of question papers, retrieval of answer scripts and the facilities for candidates.

The Chairman stated that there would be no compromise on merit, transparency or discipline during the examinations. Controller of Examinations Mubashir Saeed, while briefing the meeting, confirming that all necessary preparations for conducting the examinations are complete. He added that mobile inspectors, district vigilance committees and various inspection teams will remain active in the field.

headline: Gharo glitch adds fuel to city's water crisis
description: Gharo glitch adds fuel to city's water crisis
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Just when Karachi's prolonged water crisis showed no sign of easing, a power cable fault at the Gharo Pumping Station has dealt another blow to the city's fragile supply network, threatening to deprive several localities of around 14 million gallons of water and piling further pressure on residents already enduring weeks of shortages.

According to a spokesperson for the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation (KWSC), the electrical fault at the Gharo Pumping Station suspended power supply to the Gharo New Pump House, Gharo Old Pump House and the filtration plant, temporarily halting water supply from the facility to Karachi.

The disruption is expected to affect Port Qasim, Bin Qasim Town, Shah Faisal Town, PNS Mehran, PAF Base Faisal and the Karsaz area. The spokesperson said KWSC officials were in constant contact with K-Electric management to restore electricity and resume pumping operations.

The Gharo Pumping Station supplies around 30 million gallons of water to Karachi daily. However, the power disruption is expected to leave the city facing a shortfall of approximately 14 million gallons.

The spokesperson added that KWSC normally supplies around 650 million gallons of water to the city daily, while approximately 536 million gallons were being supplied despite the disruption. Water supply from Gharo would return to normal as soon as electricity was restored.

Meanwhile, severe shortages continue to plague several other parts of Karachi. Residents of Gulshan-e-Iqbal's Blocks 13-A, 13-B, 13-C, 13-D, 13-D1, 13-D2, 2, 4 and 5 have reported prolonged disruptions, while Tariq Road, Delhi Mercantile Society, Korangi and Landhi are also facing acute shortages.

Residents complained that the water utility had failed to restore normal supplies despite more than a month of shortages. They said prolonged disruptions, coupled with power failures at pumping stations and problems with water pipelines, had further aggravated the situation. With the metropolis already struggling to meet its water requirements, the latest disruption at Gharo has placed additional pressure on the supply network, raising fears of further shortages across Karachi.

Meanwhile, a K-Electric spokesperson said teams were working to rectify the fault that had disrupted power supply to the Gharo Pumping Station.

article_html:
GHARO:

Just when Karachi's prolonged water crisis showed no sign of easing, a power cable fault at the Gharo Pumping Station has dealt another blow to the city's fragile supply network, threatening to deprive several localities of around 14 million gallons of water and piling further pressure on residents already enduring weeks of shortages.

According to a spokesperson for the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation (KWSC), the electrical fault at the Gharo Pumping Station suspended power supply to the Gharo New Pump House, Gharo Old Pump House and the filtration plant, temporarily halting water supply from the facility to Karachi.

The disruption is expected to affect Port Qasim, Bin Qasim Town, Shah Faisal Town, PNS Mehran, PAF Base Faisal and the Karsaz area. The spokesperson said KWSC officials were in constant contact with K-Electric management to restore electricity and resume pumping operations.

The Gharo Pumping Station supplies around 30 million gallons of water to Karachi daily. However, the power disruption is expected to leave the city facing a shortfall of approximately 14 million gallons.

The spokesperson added that KWSC normally supplies around 650 million gallons of water to the city daily, while approximately 536 million gallons were being supplied despite the disruption. Water supply from Gharo would return to normal as soon as electricity was restored.

Meanwhile, severe shortages continue to plague several other parts of Karachi. Residents of Gulshan-e-Iqbal's Blocks 13-A, 13-B, 13-C, 13-D, 13-D1, 13-D2, 2, 4 and 5 have reported prolonged disruptions, while Tariq Road, Delhi Mercantile Society, Korangi and Landhi are also facing acute shortages.

Residents complained that the water utility had failed to restore normal supplies despite more than a month of shortages. They said prolonged disruptions, coupled with power failures at pumping stations and problems with water pipelines, had further aggravated the situation. With the metropolis already struggling to meet its water requirements, the latest disruption at Gharo has placed additional pressure on the supply network, raising fears of further shortages across Karachi.

Meanwhile, a K-Electric spokesperson said teams were working to rectify the fault that had disrupted power supply to the Gharo Pumping Station.

headline: SBCA invites bids for demolition of Gul Plaza
description: SBCA invites bids for demolition of Gul Plaza
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA) has invited bids for the demolition of Gul Plaza on MA Jinnah Road, setting a minimum bid of Rs40 million as it moves towards clearing the remains of the fire-ravaged commercial complex.

According to an advertisement issued by the authority, interested companies can submit their bids by November 20. The successful contractor will also be entitled to the debris and scrap recovered during the demolition.

The SBCA director of Demolition said technical and financial proposals had been invited separately, adding that preference would be given to companies with experience of demolishing at least 20 buildings. The selected contractor will be required to complete the demolition within three months, with the entire operation to be conducted under the supervision of the SBCA.

Officials said the deputy commissioner District South would decide the distribution of any goods belonging to shopkeepers recovered from the debris during the operation.

Gul Plaza was struck by a devastating fire on the night of January 17, 2026, which claimed 72 lives and destroyed more than 1,153 shops. A technical committee constituted after the incident had recommended demolishing the building in its report submitted in January. The Sindh government has also announced plans to construct a new building at the site.

headline: 'Dala culture' strikes again: family 'assaulted'
description: Complainant claims that the suspects belonged to his neighbourhood
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Complainant claims that the suspects belonged to his neighbourhood

In another alleged display of 'dala culture', a family travelling in a car was harassed and its driver assaulted by men riding in a black SUV in North Karachi, with CCTV footage of the incident emerging on Monday.

A case has been registered against four nominated suspects at the Sir Syed police station on the complaint of the victim, identified as car dealer Abdul Mateen.

The CCTV footage purportedly shows the car dealer being assaulted in front of his wife and children.In his complaint, Mateen told police that he had gone to Jauhar with his wife and child for dinner. While returning home in their car, they noticed a vehicle following them. He alleged that the occupants of a black SUV intercepted his car on a service road. Several men got out of the vehicle and began assaulting him.

The complainant claimed that the suspects belonged to his neighbourhood. He further alleged that the men threatened and intimidated him and pulled at his wife's dupatta, while the incident left his son badly frightened.

Police have registered a case against the four nominated suspects and launched a search for their arrest.

headline: Hospitals witness protest over 'harassment'
description: Hospitals witness protest over 'harassment'
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Doctors say the medical profession was already grappling with numerous administrative and professional challenges

Doctors and paramedical staff staged protests at Karachi's major public-sector hospitals, demanding protection of their professional rights, dignity and security amid growing resentment over what they described as harassment, unjustified legal action and policies imposed without consultation.

The demonstrations were held at the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC) and the National Institute of Child Health (NICH) in response to a nationwide protest call by the Pakistan Medical Association (PMA), Joint Action Committee and other medical organisations.

The protests were attended by representatives of the Young Doctors Association (YDA) Sindh and Karachi Division, along with doctors and healthcare workers from the participating hospitals.

The protesters voiced concern over what they termed unjustified registration of FIRs against doctors, legal proceedings, harassment, humiliation and character assassination. They also opposed the Federal Board of Revenue's (FBR) policy making the Point of Sale (POS) system mandatory for private clinics and healthcare facilities.

Doctors said the medical profession was already grappling with numerous administrative and professional challenges, while the threat of allegedly unfair criminal proceedings and harassment had further heightened insecurity among healthcare workers.

headline: Sindh, WB review $3.85b development portfolio
description: Sindh, WB review $3.85b development portfolio
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Billions of dollars in development funding are yet to translate into completed projects across Sindh, prompting Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah and the World Bank to review implementation delays, financial progress and procurement bottlenecks in a portfolio worth $3.849 billion.

At a high-level meeting at the Chief Minister's House on Monday, the two sides reviewed 12 ongoing projects, including 11 Investment Project Financing schemes and one Programme-for-Results project. Of the total allocation, $2.334 billion has been disbursed, while $1.571 billion remains to be released.

The meeting, chaired by CM Shah and World Bank Country Director Bolormaa Amgaabazar, also reviewed procurement activities and implementation challenges across key sectors, including water, transport, healthcare, education, agriculture and housing.

For the fiscal year 2026-27, the government has set a disbursement target of $381.2 million, with a higher target of $434.2 million. So far, $43.2 million has been disbursed.

CM Shah reaffirmed his government's commitment to accelerating implementation, removing administrative and financial bottlenecks and converting development investments into improved public services. He directed departments and project teams to take responsibility for pending actions and meet agreed deadlines.

Karachi's water and sewerage infrastructure featured prominently in the discussions, particularly the $240 million second phase of the Karachi Water and Sewerage Services Improvement Project (KWSSIP-II), linked to the K-IV water supply scheme.

Environmental and social documents for associated facilities have been submitted to the World Bank for approval. A fresh survey to reassess the Resettlement Action Plan for additional K-IV capacity is expected to begin soon. Billions of dollars in development funding are yet to translate into completed projects across Sindh, prompting Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah and the World Bank to review implementation delays, financial progress and procurement bottlenecks in a portfolio worth $3.849 billion.

He directed departments and project teams to take responsibility for pending actions and meet agreed deadlines.

The newly constructed Taj Haider Bridge was opened to traffic in October 2025, while work on the overall bridge project, including demolition of the old structure, stands at 73.9% against a target of 92.7%. headline: Court orders production of Hindu girl on Nov 23
description: Court orders production of Hindu girl on Nov 23
author: Z Ali
article_text:
The Sindh High Court, Larkana, has ordered the police to produce Hindu girl Bindiya Kumari before the court on November 23. Bindiya married to a Muslim boy after embracing Islam. Renamed as Yasmeen, Bindiya solemnized marriage with Yasir Domki last month reportedly in Bharchundi Sharif, Ghotki district. Both hail from Sibi, Balochistan.

The couple, both of whom are allegedly underage according to Kumari's parents who registered a kidnapping FIR in Sibi on October 16, have also been reportedly given protection at Bharchundi Sharif by religious influential figure and politician Pir Abdul Haq, aka Mian Mithu.

Talking to the media after the hearing at SHC Larkana bench on Monday, the minority family's law advocate Athar Solangi maintained that Kumari was 14-year-old as per her school certificate.

He recalled that the girl was allegedly kidnapped from Sibi on October 14 and two days later the incident's FIR was registered on her family's complaint at Sibi police station.

He, however, lamented that they were expecting an order from the court for early recovery of the girl, who is currently living in Sindh.

Referring to the Sindh Child Marriages Restraint Act, 2013, the lawyer contended that both the girl and the boy were underage. He also claimed that a legal marriage contract, Nikkah Nama, between the two has not been signed so far. Hindu Panchayat's local leader said Domkis should wait for her to become 18 years old before she could decide about marriage. According to him, she is a student of class nine.

Domki's lawyer said Kumari, renamed as Yasmeen, has claimed that she was 18 years old and that her decision of marriage is her free will.

headline: Forum calls for protection of Tharis' rights
description: Forum calls for protection of Tharis' rights
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Further demands included transparency in royalty and CSR funds

The Thar Citizens Forum has called for local communities' rights to be protected alongside the development of Thar coal resources. The forum's demands included emergency assistance for drought-hit areas by providing food, water, medical care, and fodder and vaccines for livestock. Adoption of a drought policy and establishment of an authority, independent testing of groundwater and the environment; and the restoration of reverse-osmosis (RO) plants also included in the demands.

The forum also called for investigations into the Danodhandal incident, compensation and rehabilitation for affected families, and the restoration of access routes. Further demands included transparency in royalty and CSR funds, protection of wildlife, measures to prevent deaths.

headline: Rs23.95b irregularities unearthed in irrigation dept
description: Rs23.95b irregularities unearthed in Irrigation Dept
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Billions of rupees meant for managing Sindh's irrigation infrastructure and executing development schemes have come under scrutiny, with an audit uncovering financial irregularities and violations of rules amounting to Rs23.95 billion in the provincial Irrigation Department during 2024-25.

From allegedly manipulated contract awards and questionable procurements to payments made in violation of prescribed procedures, a 54-point audit report has flagged a range of financial and administrative lapses, raising serious questions about the department's handling of public funds.

The Auditor General of Pakistan has forwarded the detailed report to the Sindh irrigation secretary for further action.

According to the audit findings, irregularities included the unlawful division of contracts, payments made contrary to approved rules and procedural violations in the processing and clearance of bills.

The report also pointed to alleged circumvention of mandatory procedures during the approval and execution of development projects. Certain expenditures were reportedly justified on grounds of emergency works, despite questions over their legality and the potential losses caused to the public exchequer.

The acceptance of allegedly illegal tenders and procurement in violation of prescribed regulations also came under scrutiny.

Among the issues highlighted was expenditure running into millions of rupees on filling breaches in flood embankments. The department, however, reportedly failed to provide the audit team with satisfactory legal or documentary justification for the substantial spending.

The audit authorities have recommended a transparent investigation into the reported irregularities and legal action against officials found responsible.

headline: 'President reviews development projects'
description: 'President reviews development projects'
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon has said that President Asif Ali Zardari is reviewing ongoing development schemes and public welfare projects across the province and during road visits he is personally inspecting various projects.

Sharjeel added that road, irrigation, health and education are top priority projects and officials are briefing the president on progress. Sharjeel further mentioned, the president has directed authorities to accelerate development work and address public concerns promptly.

Development activities are continuing across all districts in line with the president's instructions, with special focus on providing basic services to the people in both urban and rural areas.

Meanwhile, in a statement, the senior minister said, improving healthcare, education and infrastructure remains a top priority for the provincial government, adding that there would be no compromise on providing people with essential services.

He said, the government is working to upgrade public hospitals by providing modern equipment, medicines and improved treatment facilities. Specialist medical institutions are also providing care for complex conditions, including heart and kidney diseases and cancer.

He said expanding access to modern healthcare in rural areas was a priority, so residents in both urban and rural communities could receive comparable services.

headline: Pollution touches hazardous level
description: Pollution touches hazardous level
author: ADNAN LODHI
article_text:
Smog continued to blanket Lahore as the city topped IQAir's ranking of the world's most polluted major cities, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 298, while Punjab's environmental monitoring dashboard placed Dera Ghazi Khan, Kot Addu and Nankana Sahib at the highest reported reading of 500.

According to the latest IQAir figures, Lahore was followed by Kolkata with an AQI of 189 and Delhi at 186.

However, the Punjab AQI dashboard placed Dera Ghazi Khan, Kot Addu and Nankana Sahib jointly at the top of its city ranking, each recording an AQI of 500.

Lahore ranked fourth in the provincial list with an AQI of 433, followed by Sheikhupura at 348 and Kasur 343. Sahiwal recorded 338, Wazirabad 326 and Khushab 310, while Faisalabad registered 307.

The figures indicate that severe air pollution is not confined to Lahore, with several other cities across Punjab also recording very high readings.

The provincial dashboard and IQAir use separate monitoring networks and reporting systems.

Area-wise readings for Lahore earlier in the day showed particularly high pollution levels in several localities. Iqbal Town recorded an AQI of 902, followed by Paragon City at 698, Chaman Park 619, Barki Road 569, Model Town 471, DHA Phase V 412, Bedian Road 358 and Askari 10 recorded 298.

Meteorological information indicated dry weather in the city, with no rain forecast. The maximum temperature was recorded at 29°C. Humidity stood at 65 per cent, while wind speed was recorded at 3km per hour.

The lack of rainfall and slow winds can limit the dispersal of pollutants, although changes in weather and emissions will influence how air quality develops.

Residents were advised to avoid unnecessary outdoor activities and take precautions when going outside. People with respiratory conditions should be particularly careful during periods of heavy pollution.

Lahore had plunged deeper into smog in the morning with the AQI soaring above 500 and fine particulate matter (PM2.5) reaching 343 micrograms per cubic metre at 8am, exposing millions of residents to dangerously polluted air.

The readings were among the most alarming reported so far during the ongoing smog season.

Smog blanketed several parts of the city and adjoining localities.

Gujranwala recorded an AQI of 606, Faisalabad and Multan 310, and Sialkot 260, highlighting a growing regional air pollution emergency.

Lahore's pollution levels also placed it at the top of the global major cities' pollution ranking in the morning.

The deterioration raised questions about the effectiveness of the government's anti-smog actions as crop residue burning, industrial and vehicular emissions as well as construction dust continued to aggravate pollution across Lahore and neighbouring districts.

Sheikhupura, Kasur, Gujranwala, Nankana Sahib and several other districts were also affected.

Industrial fuel consumption, brick kilns, stubble burning, waste disposal practices and emissions from transport add to the pollution.

According to a website, the United States National Aeronautics and Space Administration satellites detected 13,241 fire spots in Punjab between October 1 and 29.

headline: Deficient waste companies face termination
description: Deficient waste companies face termination
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has set a 15-day deadline to ensure improvement in cleanliness across the province.

She was chairing a meeting to review the performance of the Suthra Punjab programme, during which a decision was taken to terminate the services of solid waste management companies over unsatisfactory cleanliness arrangements and launch self-operation in Lahore, Faisalabad, Gujranwala, Multan and Dera Ghazi Khan.

The chief minister expressed concern over dust and dirt on roads across the province. She ordered daily washing of main roads.

She directed authorities to impose fines on those found littering roads after the cleaning. Penalisation for dumping garbage in vegetable, fruit, grain and other markets was also ordered.

Targets were set in the meeting for ensuring adequate human resources and machinery in every district.

The chief minister ordered the cleaning of the villages every alternate day.

She instructed the deputy and assistant commissioners to hold weekly meetings with field monitoring officers and ordered the formulation of Key Performance Indicators to assess them.

Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz also ordered timely payment of salaries to sanitation workers in every locality. She sought details from all DCs regarding machinery required for sanitation, along with comprehensive record of savings achieved through self-operation.

The participants also discussed imposition of fine on owners of vacant plots where garbage is found.

The DCs of Multan, Rajanpur, Dera Ghazi Khan, Hafizabad, Muzaffargarh and other districts presented their reports. The CM directed them to physically verify the equipment in their districts.

headline: City records 112 suicides in 10 months
description: City records 112 suicides in 10 months
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Figures, covering January 1 to October 31, showed that 87 men and 25 women died by suicide

At least 112 people took their own lives in the city during the past 10 months of 2026, according to figures released by the Edhi Foundation, with men accounting for the majority of reported deaths.

The figures, covering January 1 to October 31, showed that 87 men and 25 women died by suicide during the period.

The incidents were linked to various factors, including poverty, failed relationships, domestic disputes and other personal difficulties.

The monthly figures showed fluctuations in the number of reported deaths throughout the year. January and July recorded the highest monthly toll, with 14 deaths each, while June had the lowest figure of five.

In January, 11 men and three women died by suicide. February witnessed the death of 11 men and a woman. March saw five men and a woman ending their lives, while in April the deaths of nine men and a woman were recorded.

headline: Pakistan, Tajikistan to boost trade ties
description: Toir says direct links among manufacturers, exporters and buyers could help businesses explore new markets
author: Khawar Randhawa
article_text:
Toir says direct links among manufacturers, exporters and buyers could help businesses explore new markets

Tajikistan's Ambassador Sharifzoda Yousuf Toir has called for stronger economic engagement between Pakistan and Tajikistan, saying the two countries have significant potential to diversify bilateral trade, promote investment and expand business-to-business cooperation.

Speaking at the Pakistan Textile Exporters Association (PTEA), the ambassador said both countries were committed to strengthening the economic dimension of their relationship and translating their longstanding ties into tangible benefits for businesses.

He said bilateral trade stood at $43 million in 2025, while the two governments had set a target of increasing it to $200 million over the next three years.

Achieving the target would require sustained engagement, stronger commercial links and closer coordination between businesses and relevant institutions in both countries.

Highlighting opportunities for cooperation between the textile sectors of the two countries, Toir said direct links among manufacturers, exporters and buyers could help businesses explore new markets, identify complementary capabilities and establish long-term commercial partnerships.

He stressed the need to improve exporters' access to information about tariffs, product standards, buyer requirements and transport arrangements.

headline: Man held for harassment, blackmail
description: Man held for harassment, blackmail
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) has arrested a man for allegedly harassing and blackmailing a woman through WhatsApp and registered a case against him.

Acting on the directions of Additional Director Chaudhry Ijaz Ahmad, an NCCIA raiding team, led by SHO Aamir Sultan, arrested the suspect, identified as Asim Mustafa.

Officials said they had recovered a mobile phone from the suspect, which allegedly contained threatening messages and objectionable videos of the complainant.

The NCCIA's cybercrime police station registered a case against the suspect under Sections 20, 21 and 24 of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) 2016, as amended in 2025.

Further investigation is under way, with officials examining the digital evidence recovered during the operation.

NCCIA officials said action against those involved in online harassment, blackmail and the intimidation or exploitation of citizens through digital platforms would continue without discrimination.

headline: 464 die in Punjab road crashes in October
description: 464 die in Punjab road crashes in October
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
At least 464 people were killed and 23,543 seriously injured in 44,797 road traffic crashes across Punjab in October 2026, with motorcycles involved in nearly three-quarters of the incidents, according to Rescue 1122.

Expressing concern over the figures, Emergency Services Department Secretary Dr Rizwan Naseer called for greater attention to road safety, particularly among motorcyclists.

He urged riders to keep to the left side of the road and maintain speeds below 50 kilometres per hour, warning that excessive speed increased the risk of fatal accidents.

The figures were shared during a monthly review of the emergency operational performance of Rescue 1122 districts across the province.

According to the department, its teams responded to 231,056 emergencies during October and rescued 233,210 people.

These included road accidents, medical emergencies, fires, drowning incidents and other rescue operations.

The department recorded 1,726 fire emergencies and 94 drowning incidents during the month.

The head of operations informed the meeting that accidents and other injuries accounted for the largest category of emergencies, with 59,325 cases. These were followed by 42,813 cardiovascular emergencies, 31,301 gastrointestinal cases and 22,605 respiratory emergencies.

The data also included 17,853 neurological emergencies, 15,212 fever cases, 7,954 gynaecological and obstetric emergencies and 7,498 urinary cases.

Rescue 1122 additionally handled 6,924 fire and rescue emergencies, 5,275 diabetic cases, 4,915 psychosocial emergencies, 4,227 cases involving back and joint pain, 4,195 crime-related emergencies and 379 allergy cases.

Lahore recorded the highest number of road crashes, with 7,874 incidents involving 8,833 motorcycles. Multan reported 2,838 accidents involving 3,312 motorcycles, while Faisalabad recorded 2,615 crashes involving 2,896 motorcycles.

Gujranwala reported 2,092 accidents involving 2,250 motorcycles, followed by Sheikhupura with 1,714 crashes involving 1,706 motorcycles.

Taunsa Sharif recorded the lowest number, with 142 accidents involving 160 motorcycles.

Fires were also concentrated in major districts. Lahore reported 357 incidents, followed by Faisalabad with 122, Rawalpindi with 116 and Multan with 109. Sheikhupura recorded 66 fire incidents and Gujranwala 62.

Dr Rizwan chaired the monthly review meeting on Monday, which was attended by directors of emergency services, heads of wings and the provincial monitoring officer.

District emergency officers joined through video link.

During the meeting, district officers briefed the secretary on their operational performance, major emergencies, response efforts, challenges and lessons learnt.

Dr Rizwan said the figures underlined the need to strengthen road safety measures and improve public awareness, particularly among motorcyclists.

article_html:
LAHORE:

At least 464 people were killed and 23,543 seriously injured in 44,797 road traffic crashes across Punjab in October 2026, with motorcycles involved in nearly three-quarters of the incidents, according to Rescue 1122.

Expressing concern over the figures, Emergency Services Department Secretary Dr Rizwan Naseer called for greater attention to road safety, particularly among motorcyclists.

He urged riders to keep to the left side of the road and maintain speeds below 50 kilometres per hour, warning that excessive speed increased the risk of fatal accidents.

The figures were shared during a monthly review of the emergency operational performance of Rescue 1122 districts across the province.

According to the department, its teams responded to 231,056 emergencies during October and rescued 233,210 people.

These included road accidents, medical emergencies, fires, drowning incidents and other rescue operations.

The department recorded 1,726 fire emergencies and 94 drowning incidents during the month.

The head of operations informed the meeting that accidents and other injuries accounted for the largest category of emergencies, with 59,325 cases. These were followed by 42,813 cardiovascular emergencies, 31,301 gastrointestinal cases and 22,605 respiratory emergencies.

The data also included 17,853 neurological emergencies, 15,212 fever cases, 7,954 gynaecological and obstetric emergencies and 7,498 urinary cases.

Rescue 1122 additionally handled 6,924 fire and rescue emergencies, 5,275 diabetic cases, 4,915 psychosocial emergencies, 4,227 cases involving back and joint pain, 4,195 crime-related emergencies and 379 allergy cases.

Lahore recorded the highest number of road crashes, with 7,874 incidents involving 8,833 motorcycles. Multan reported 2,838 accidents involving 3,312 motorcycles, while Faisalabad recorded 2,615 crashes involving 2,896 motorcycles.

Gujranwala reported 2,092 accidents involving 2,250 motorcycles, followed by Sheikhupura with 1,714 crashes involving 1,706 motorcycles.

Taunsa Sharif recorded the lowest number, with 142 accidents involving 160 motorcycles.

Fires were also concentrated in major districts. Lahore reported 357 incidents, followed by Faisalabad with 122, Rawalpindi with 116 and Multan with 109. Sheikhupura recorded 66 fire incidents and Gujranwala 62.

Dr Rizwan chaired the monthly review meeting on Monday, which was attended by directors of emergency services, heads of wings and the provincial monitoring officer.

District emergency officers joined through video link.

During the meeting, district officers briefed the secretary on their operational performance, major emergencies, response efforts, challenges and lessons learnt.

Dr Rizwan said the figures underlined the need to strengthen road safety measures and improve public awareness, particularly among motorcyclists.

headline: Suspect identified in murder case
description: Suspect identified in murder case
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Victim's family has taken custody of both vehicles seized by police

The identification parade of Umer Khalid, the suspect arrested for allegedly killing industrialist Rehan Ashraf during a vehicle snatching incident, has been completed at the District Jail Faisalabad.

The complainant, the victim's brother Hassan Ashraf, and two witnesses identified the suspect before a judge, police sources said.

The suspect will now be handed over to Sadar police on physical remand for interrogation after the court's formal order is received.

Police sources said Hassan Ashraf and the two witnesses, Amjad and Ikram, reached the district jail at 11am on November 2. Judge Mubashir Awan, appointed to oversee the identification parade, arrived at 11.30am.

Jail officials had arranged three rows, each comprising six suspects, for identification. Hassan Ashraf and the two witnesses identified Umer Khalid by placing their hands on his shoulder, saying he was the man who had allegedly killed Rehan Ashraf.

The witnesses maintained that the suspect had shot the industrialist dead while fleeing after snatching his vehicle and being pursued by the victim.

Meanwhile, the victim's family has taken custody of both vehicles seized by police.

headline: Counterfeit salt, snacks seized
description: Counterfeit salt, snacks seized
author: APP
article_text:
Team also seized the prohibited Chinese salt during the operation

The Punjab Food Authority (PFA) has seized 1,152 kilogrammes of counterfeit snack packets and 75 kilogrammes of prohibited Chinese salt during a raid on a papad factory in Al-Khalil Colony near WAPDA Grid Station on Bahawalpur Bypass.

The raid was conducted as part of an ongoing crackdown on manufacturers producing counterfeit and potentially harmful snacks for children, on the directions of PFA Director General Raja Mansoor Ahmed. According to the authority, its food safety team inspected the factory and recovered snack packets bearing counterfeit branding of a well-known international company. The team also seized the prohibited Chinese salt during the operation.

The products were allegedly being manufactured for sale using fake labels and branding designed to imitate established brands and mislead consumers.

headline: Long wait ends as lawyer meets jailed Imran, Bushra
description: Long wait ends as lawyer meets jailed Imran, Bushra
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
After a gap of several months, government authorities on Monday allowed Barrister Salman Safdar to meet his incarcerated clients, former prime minister and PTI founder Imran Khan and his spouse Bushra Bibi, at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail.

Safdar, who serves as a lead counsel in several cases involving Imran and Bushra, later published a brief post on X on Monday night, stating that the meeting facilitated by the jail administration started at around 4:30 pm and continued for 40 minutes.

According to Safdar, he was permitted to meet the PTI founder and his wife- despite repeated requests and applications, respectively- after seven and eleven months.

"[The 40-minute] session was insufficient to cover all cases/legal matters," he said.

Safdar stated that both the former prime minister and his wife briefed him on their health conditions and living conditions in the jail.

"[They also] gave [me] fresh instructions on some legal matters and cases," he added, without giving any specific details about the health condition of the couple.

Talking to a news outlet, PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said the meeting between Imran-Bushra and Safdar took place in connection with a number of applications filed in courts seeking a meeting with the jailed party founder and his wife.

Replying to a question, Akram said no political issues were discussed during the meeting. Safdar, he said, spoke about the cases and asked about future strategy. Asked about Imran's health, the PTI official replied that health issues were discussed, but the party would only speak about the legal cases.

Barrister Salman Safdar last met Imran Khan on April 9 after the Islamabad High Court (IHC) allowed him to discuss the proceedings of the £190m case with Imran. However, in that meeting- which had lasted 60 minutes- the counsel was not allowed to meet Bushra Bibi.

In a brief statement issued after the meeting, Safdar had claimed that the PTI founder and his wife were kept in solitary confinement for almost 24 hours a day, with no access to books, television, family, or lawyers.

While hearing a set of pleas including those related to Imran's medical treatment and his meetings with family members and lawyers, the Supreme Court on August 18 ordered that the PTI founder be shifted to Islamabad's Shifa International Hospital within two days for medical examination and treatment.

A three-member bench comprising Justice Shahid Waheed, Justice Naeem Akhter Afghan and Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim also ordered the government to constitute a specialised medical board for Imran's care.

On the same day, Imran Khan's sister Noreen Niazi also met the PTI founder at Adiala Jail after a gap of around nine months. The meeting lasted approximately 15 minutes.

However, on August 20, Imran Khan was taken to Islamabad's Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), rather than Shifa International Hospital, for a medical examination before being declared medically fit and returned to Adiala Jail.

According to Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, Imran was taken to PIMS instead of Shifa "in view of the security situation created by PTI workers on the route to and outside Shifa Hospital", adding that doctors from Shifa were also present during the examination.

On the same day, August 20, the federal government also petitioned the Supreme Court to review and recall its August 18 order, arguing that the directive was discriminatory and issued in violation of prison rules and principles of natural justice.

Imran Khan has been detained at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail for over three years.

Authorities have denied weekly meetings between Imran and his family and lawyers since December last year. In the meantime, the former PM has also developed medical conditions affecting his eyesight.
