RAWALPINDI:

After a gap of several months, government authorities on Monday allowed Barrister Salman Safdar to meet his incarcerated clients, former prime minister and PTI founder Imran Khan and his spouse Bushra Bibi, at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail.

Safdar, who serves as a lead counsel in several cases involving Imran and Bushra, later published a brief post on X on Monday night, stating that the meeting facilitated by the jail administration started at around 4:30 pm and continued for 40 minutes.

According to Safdar, he was permitted to meet the PTI founder and his wife- despite repeated requests and applications, respectively- after seven and eleven months.

"[The 40-minute] session was insufficient to cover all cases/legal matters," he said.

Safdar stated that both the former prime minister and his wife briefed him on their health conditions and living conditions in the jail.

"[They also] gave [me] fresh instructions on some legal matters and cases," he added, without giving any specific details about the health condition of the couple.

Talking to a news outlet, PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said the meeting between Imran-Bushra and Safdar took place in connection with a number of applications filed in courts seeking a meeting with the jailed party founder and his wife.

Replying to a question, Akram said no political issues were discussed during the meeting. Safdar, he said, spoke about the cases and asked about future strategy. Asked about Imran's health, the PTI official replied that health issues were discussed, but the party would only speak about the legal cases.

Barrister Salman Safdar last met Imran Khan on April 9 after the Islamabad High Court (IHC) allowed him to discuss the proceedings of the £190m case with Imran. However, in that meeting- which had lasted 60 minutes- the counsel was not allowed to meet Bushra Bibi.

In a brief statement issued after the meeting, Safdar had claimed that the PTI founder and his wife were kept in solitary confinement for almost 24 hours a day, with no access to books, television, family, or lawyers.

While hearing a set of pleas including those related to Imran's medical treatment and his meetings with family members and lawyers, the Supreme Court on August 18 ordered that the PTI founder be shifted to Islamabad's Shifa International Hospital within two days for medical examination and treatment.

A three-member bench comprising Justice Shahid Waheed, Justice Naeem Akhter Afghan and Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim also ordered the government to constitute a specialised medical board for Imran's care.

On the same day, Imran Khan's sister Noreen Niazi also met the PTI founder at Adiala Jail after a gap of around nine months. The meeting lasted approximately 15 minutes.

However, on August 20, Imran Khan was taken to Islamabad's Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), rather than Shifa International Hospital, for a medical examination before being declared medically fit and returned to Adiala Jail.

According to Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, Imran was taken to PIMS instead of Shifa "in view of the security situation created by PTI workers on the route to and outside Shifa Hospital", adding that doctors from Shifa were also present during the examination.

On the same day, August 20, the federal government also petitioned the Supreme Court to review and recall its August 18 order, arguing that the directive was discriminatory and issued in violation of prison rules and principles of natural justice.

Imran Khan has been detained at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail for over three years.

Authorities have denied weekly meetings between Imran and his family and lawyers since December last year. In the meantime, the former PM has also developed medical conditions affecting his eyesight.

headline: Refineries to shoulder Rs15b fuel burden
description: Refineries to shoulder Rs15b fuel burden
author: Shahbaz Rana
article_text:
Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said on Monday that a Pakistan-bound LNG cargo ship was attacked before it entered the Strait of Hormuz but did not name the culprits, as he formally announced to pass on the impact of Rs15 per liter petroleum levy to oil refineries to keep petrol prices relatively lower.

"The LNG-ship was hit before it entered the Strait of Harmuz," said Ali, while addressing a press conference along with Information Minister Attaullah Tarar. The information minister urged the media to avoid any speculation about the perpetrators and said that the government would share only the verified information.

"Rest assured there are no shortages of the supplies. It is a sensitive time and one should avoid speculation," he said, while responding to a question how the ship was attacked when Pakistan had gotten clearance from Iran.

Qatar and Saudi Arabia have condemned the attack on the LNG tanker, calling it a "dangerous act" that threatened the security of global energy supplies.

Pakistan had negotiated with Iran to secure safe passage for LNG carrier Al Mayeda. The Qatari foreign ministry said it had initiated the necessary investigations to determine the circumstances of the incident and identify those responsible for the attack on the vessel.

The information minister did not respond to questions about the opening or closing of Pakistan-Iran border for trade but said that in this case also the speculations should be avoided.

Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of approximately Rs15 per litre or Rs15 billion for one month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than what it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

The impact of the Rs15 per litre burden shifting from consumer to oil refineries has already been passed in Friday's price determination.

He said that the arrangement had been implemented from Friday after Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif decided to pass on the partial impact of the levy to oil refineries. "The oil refineries' three-month profits are even more than their annual profits of the last year," said Malik.

Till now the government was reluctant to admit that the oil refineries were earning exorbitant profits and there was a need to change the pricing formula. "I am grateful to all the refineries that saw the public is in difficulty and with the government's help increased their throughput," the minister said.

"They were requested to take a step to support the public during this difficult time, and I am glad that they listened to us the Rs15 increase that was coming in the petrol prices on Friday, they helped the government with that and because of that we were able to maintain the price.

The government is still charging Rs80 per liter levy out of the Rs378 petrol price but now the Rs14.71 per liter levy will be paid by these refineries.

The federal cabinet on Friday approved that the import price of petrol may be determined on the basis of the actual import cost of the relevant PSO cargo. Where the actual import cost is unavailable for the relevant daily pricing, the premium, incidentals and customs duty of the last available cargo may be used to determine the import price.

The refineries will be entitled to ex-refinery price of petrol calculated by fixing premium, incidentals and customs duty at level of price effective for 7 March 2026 (pre-war) for next 30 days. The difference between the import price determined and the ex-refinery price shall be surrendered by the refineries under Petroleum Levy head of account.

The resulting benefit from the adjustment in petroleum levy will be passed on to petrol consumers only through a corresponding reduction in the price of petrol.

Malik said that more improvement would be seen by the public, expressing his gratitude to the refineries for standing with the government to provide assistance to the public during a time that had caused everyone difficulties - even the government as it struggled to procure oil at increasing prices.

He added that before the crisis, the premium of the refineries was $5 per barrel, and even today a $20 limit had been established. He further said that the government would have to step in and protect the public in case of further difficulties.

To a question regarding a delay in finalising 16 to 22 LNG cargoes to meet winter needs, the petroleum minister said that the prime minister and a few friends had a view that the difference between the Qatar LNG and the one bought from the open market was high.

Based on the three-time meal supply of gas to residential consumers, the government has made arrangements to meet the requirements of November, said Malik. He said that the decisions were being made to meet the requirements for the months of December and January.

The information minister said that the fuel subsidy scheme for the motorcyclists and car owners would continue. So far Rs27 billion have been disbursed under the scheme and 15 million beneficiaries have registered for it.

Tarar also defended the ad-hoc appointment of Establishment Secretary Nabeel Awan as acting Chairman Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra). It does not matter whether the OGRA chairman is acting or permanent but he was doing a great job and would continue serving as the OGRA chairman, said Tarar.

The information minister urged the media to avoid any speculation about the perpetrators and said that the government would share only the verified information.

"Rest assured there are no shortages of the supplies. It is a sensitive time and one should avoid speculation," he said, while responding to a question how the ship was attacked when Pakistan had gotten clearance from Iran.

Qatar and Saudi Arabia have condemned the attack on the LNG tanker, calling it a "dangerous act" that threatened the security of global energy supplies.

Pakistan had negotiated with Iran to secure safe passage for LNG carrier Al Mayeda. The Qatari foreign ministry said it had initiated the necessary investigations to determine the circumstances of the incident and identify those responsible for the attack on the vessel.

The information minister did not respond to questions about the opening or closing of Pakistan-Iran border for trade but said that in this case also the speculations should be avoided.

Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of approximately Rs15 per litre or Rs15 billion for one month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than what it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

The impact of the Rs15 per litre burden shifting from consumer to oil refineries has already been passed in Friday's price determination.

He said that the arrangement had been implemented from Friday after Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif decided to pass on the partial impact of the levy to oil refineries. "The oil refineries' three-month profits are even more than their annual profits of the last year," said Malik.

Till now the government was reluctant to admit that the oil refineries were earning exorbitant profits and there was a need to change the pricing formula. "I am grateful to all the refineries that saw the public is in difficulty and with the government's help increased their throughput," the minister said.

"They were requested to take a step to support the public during this difficult time, and I am glad that they listened to us the Rs15 increase that was coming in the petrol prices on Friday, they helped the government with that and because of that we were able to maintain the price.

The government is still charging Rs80 per liter levy out of the Rs378 petrol price but now the Rs14.71 per liter levy will be paid by these refineries.

The federal cabinet on Friday approved that the import price of petrol may be determined on the basis of the actual import cost of the relevant PSO cargo. Where the actual import cost is unavailable for the relevant daily pricing, the premium, incidentals and customs duty of the last available cargo may be used to determine the import price.

The refineries will be entitled to ex-refinery price of petrol calculated by fixing premium, incidentals and customs duty at level of price effective for 7 March 2026 (pre-war) for next 30 days. The difference between the import price determined and the ex-refinery price shall be surrendered by the refineries under Petroleum Levy head of account.

The resulting benefit from the adjustment in petroleum levy will be passed on to petrol consumers only through a corresponding reduction in the price of petrol.

Malik said that more improvement would be seen by the public, expressing his gratitude to the refineries for standing with the government to provide assistance to the public during a time that had caused everyone difficulties - even the government as it struggled to procure oil at increasing prices.

He added that before the crisis, the premium of the refineries was $5 per barrel, and even today a $20 limit had been established. He further said that the government would have to step in and protect the public in case of further difficulties.

To a question regarding a delay in finalising 16 to 22 LNG cargoes to meet winter needs, the petroleum minister said that the prime minister and a few friends had a view that the difference between the Qatar LNG and the one bought from the open market was high.

Based on the three-time meal supply of gas to residential consumers, the government has made arrangements to meet the requirements of November, said Malik. He said that the decisions were being made to meet the requirements for the months of December and January.

The information minister said that the fuel subsidy scheme for the motorcyclists and car owners would continue. So far Rs27 billion have been disbursed under the scheme and 15 million beneficiaries have registered for it.

Tarar also defended the ad-hoc appointment of Establishment Secretary Nabeel Awan as acting Chairman Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra). It does not matter whether the OGRA chairman is acting or permanent but he was doing a great job and would continue serving as the OGRA chairman, said Tarar.

headline: LHC orders jail meeting for Noreen
description: LHC orders jail meeting for Noreen
author: Rana Yasif
article_text:
The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Monday ordered jail authorities to arrange a one-hour meeting between Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan's sister Noreen Niazi and her two daughters at 10am on Tuesday, while summoning the Lahore Deputy Commissioner in person to explain the extension of detention orders against Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khanum.

Imran's sisters were detained in September under Section 3 of the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance, 1960, as the PTI prepared for a planned protest march towards Islamabad. Aleema was detained on September 20, while Uzma and Noreen were taken into custody on September 21. Their initial detention orders were issued for 30 days. The orders were later extended another 30 days.

Justice Abher Gul Khan issued the directions while hearing petitions filed by Sakina Niazi and Shahraiz challenging the extension orders in detention of three sisters of Imran Khan and further seeking permission for the detained sisters to meet their family members.

The court directed the petitioners' counsel to submit an application to the Lahore DC seeking permission for the meeting and ordered the deputy commissioner to ensure that the daughters were allowed to meet their mother at the jail for one hour.

The court also summoned the DC Lahore in person on November 4 in connection with the extension of detention orders against Noreen and Uzma.

Meanwhile, the hearing of the petition challenging the extension of Aleema Khanum's detention was adjourned until next week.

During the proceedings, the Punjab Home Secretary submitted a report in compliance with the court's earlier directions. The Punjab government's counsel informed the court that Noreen had received medical treatment at a hospital and was subsequently shifted back to jail on the advice of doctors.

The government lawyer further submitted that Noreen's daughter, Hajra Niazi, had already been allowed to meet her mother on October 29 during her hospital treatment.

Earlier, the court had sought reports from the Punjab home secretary and jail authorities on the continued detention of the three sisters, as well as Noreen's reported illness and the denial of family meetings with the detained women.

Justice Abher Gul Khan, while hearing petitions filed by Sakina Niazi and Shahraiz, directed the home secretary to submit a report on the extension. The court also sought a report from jail authorities on Noreen's health and directed the Inspector General of Prisons Mian Salik Jalal to submit a report on permission for the detained sisters to meet their family members.

The court had adjourned further proceedings on all petitions until 2pm today.

During the hearing, the petitioners' counsel Rana Mudassar Umar informed the court that Noreen was seriously ill and had been admitted to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC). He also filed an application seeking the court's intervention over her medical condition.

The petitions stated that the deputy commissioner had issued a notification on October 7 extending the detention of the three women after the completion of their initial 30-day detention. The petitioners challenged the notification as illegal, arguing that the extension had been issued unlawfully. They further alleged that the detained women had not been allowed to meet their family members or legal counsel.

They asked the court to declare the October 7 notification extending their detention illegal.

Meanwhile, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, speaking to the media at the LHC, alleged that Aleema and her driver had been arrested before the detention notification was issued. He said even the driver, who had been working on daily wages, had been taken into custody.

Expressing concern over the difficulties in securing meetings with the detained women through court intervention, Raja said he was compelled to acknowledge that access to detainees had become increasingly difficult.

"Anyone can be picked up at any time, and courts are unable to deliver justice," he said, adding that colonial-era laws were being used to curtail citizens' freedoms. He maintained that courts were helpless under the prevailing circumstances, despite earlier judgements delivered by an independent judiciary.

Raja also said the PTI did not control social media activities but would continue to hold protests and inform the public about political and national issues. Alleging that people taking to the streets were being fired upon, he said his party would continue to raise its voice for the supremacy of the Constitution and the rule of law.

He said highlighting issues such as inflation and unemployment was the responsibility of every political party, adding that political parties should raise their voices for the protection of constitutional rights. Raja maintained that PTI founder Imran Khan was behind bars for seeking protection of these very public rights.

LAHORE:

The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Monday ordered jail authorities to arrange a one-hour meeting between Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan's sister Noreen Niazi and her two daughters at 10am on Tuesday, while summoning the Lahore Deputy Commissioner in person to explain the extension of detention orders against Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khanum.

Imran's sisters were detained in September under Section 3 of the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance, 1960, as the PTI prepared for a planned protest march towards Islamabad. Aleema was detained on September 20, while Uzma and Noreen were taken into custody on September 21. Their initial detention orders were issued for 30 days. The orders were later extended another 30 days.

Justice Abher Gul Khan issued the directions while hearing petitions filed by Sakina Niazi and Shahraiz challenging the extension orders in detention of three sisters of Imran Khan and further seeking permission for the detained sisters to meet their family members.

The court directed the petitioners' counsel to submit an application to the Lahore DC seeking permission for the meeting and ordered the deputy commissioner to ensure that the daughters were allowed to meet their mother at the jail for one hour.

The court also summoned the DC Lahore in person on November 4 in connection with the extension of detention orders against Noreen and Uzma.

Meanwhile, the hearing of the petition challenging the extension of Aleema Khanum's detention was adjourned until next week.

During the proceedings, the Punjab Home Secretary submitted a report in compliance with the court's earlier directions. The Punjab government's counsel informed the court that Noreen had received medical treatment at a hospital and was subsequently shifted back to jail on the advice of doctors.

The government lawyer further submitted that Noreen's daughter, Hajra Niazi, had already been allowed to meet her mother on October 29 during her hospital treatment.

Earlier, the court had sought reports from the Punjab home secretary and jail authorities on the continued detention of the three sisters, as well as Noreen's reported illness and the denial of family meetings with the detained women.

Justice Abher Gul Khan, while hearing petitions filed by Sakina Niazi and Shahraiz, directed the home secretary to submit a report on the extension. The court also sought a report from jail authorities on Noreen's health and directed the Inspector General of Prisons Mian Salik Jalal to submit a report on permission for the detained sisters to meet their family members.

The court had adjourned further proceedings on all petitions until 2pm today.

During the hearing, the petitioners' counsel Rana Mudassar Umar informed the court that Noreen was seriously ill and had been admitted to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC). He also filed an application seeking the court's intervention over her medical condition.

The petitions stated that the deputy commissioner had issued a notification on October 7 extending the detention of the three women after the completion of their initial 30-day detention. The petitioners challenged the notification as illegal, arguing that the extension had been issued unlawfully. They further alleged that the detained women had not been allowed to meet their family members or legal counsel.

They asked the court to declare the October 7 notification extending their detention illegal.

Meanwhile, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, speaking to the media at the LHC, alleged that Aleema and her driver had been arrested before the detention notification was issued. He said even the driver, who had been working on daily wages, had been taken into custody.

Expressing concern over the difficulties in securing meetings with the detained women through court intervention, Raja said he was compelled to acknowledge that access to detainees had become increasingly difficult.

"Anyone can be picked up at any time, and courts are unable to deliver justice," he said, adding that colonial-era laws were being used to curtail citizens' freedoms. He maintained that courts were helpless under the prevailing circumstances, despite earlier judgements delivered by an independent judiciary.

Raja also said the PTI did not control social media activities but would continue to hold protests and inform the public about political and national issues. Alleging that people taking to the streets were being fired upon, he said his party would continue to raise its voice for the supremacy of the Constitution and the rule of law.

He said highlighting issues such as inflation and unemployment was the responsibility of every political party, adding that political parties should raise their voices for the protection of constitutional rights. Raja maintained that PTI founder Imran Khan was behind bars for seeking protection of these very public rights.

The court had adjourned further proceedings on all petitions until 2pm today.

During the hearing, the petitioners' counsel Rana Mudassar Umar informed the court that Noreen was seriously ill and had been admitted to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC). He also filed an application seeking the court's intervention over her medical condition.

The petitions stated that the deputy commissioner had issued a notification on October 7 extending the detention of the three women after the completion of their initial 30-day detention. The petitioners challenged the notification as illegal, arguing that the extension had been issued unlawfully. They further alleged that the detained women had not been allowed to meet their family members or legal counsel.
They asked the court to declare the October 7 notification extending their detention illegal.

Meanwhile, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, speaking to the media at the LHC, alleged that Aleema and her driver had been arrested before the detention notification was issued. He said even the driver, who had been working on daily wages, had been taken into custody.

Expressing concern over the difficulties in securing meetings with the detained women through court intervention, Raja said he was compelled to acknowledge that access to detainees had become increasingly difficult.

"Anyone can be picked up at any time, and courts are unable to deliver justice," he said, adding that colonial-era laws were being used to curtail citizens' freedoms. He maintained that courts were helpless under the prevailing circumstances, despite earlier judgements delivered by an independent judiciary.

Raja also said the PTI did not control social media activities but would continue to hold protests and inform the public about political and national issues. Alleging that people taking to the streets were being fired upon, he said his party would continue to raise its voice for the supremacy of the Constitution and the rule of law.

He said highlighting issues such as inflation and unemployment was the responsibility of every political party, adding that political parties should raise their voices for the protection of constitutional rights. Raja maintained that PTI founder Imran Khan was behind bars for seeking protection of these very public rights.

headline: Candidates make final push for US midterms
description: Candidates make final push for US midterms
author: AFP
article_text:
Democrats sought to contain a rift in Michigan's US Senate race after one of their own crossed party lines to endorse the Republican, while President Donald Trump pressed his legal efforts on Monday to intervene in ballot-counting as ?both parties made their closing arguments a day before midterm elections that will determine control of Congress.

Over a fast-moving weekend, US Representative Haley Stevens, who lost the Michigan Democratic Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed in a bitter contest, suddenly switched to backing Republican Mike Rogers and appeared with him at a Detroit church.

The race is critical to Democrats' hopes ?of ending the 53-47 Senate majority hold of Trump's Republicans in Tuesday's vote.

Stevens' Sunday surprise came the same day a federal judge dismissed a US Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of election results in Alaska if Republican incumbent Senator Dan S Sullivan narrowly loses in the battleground state.

An undeterred Trump, who ?has been holding daily rallies around the country for Republican candidates, filed an emergency request with the US Supreme Court on Monday to temporarily block California from counting mail-in ballots from more than 20,000 registered voters who federal officials allege are likely non-US citizens.

California said the lawsuit could disenfranchise 20,000 voters based on vague accusations and that the administration's process for identifying noncitizens was flawed and prone to error.

The president, who continues to falsely claim that his loss to Joe Biden in 2020 was caused by widespread fraud, was due to deliver remarks at 2pm ET (1900 GMT) at the belated reopening of Washington's Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

An earlier renovation as part of his ?beautification efforts for the US capital was botched by contractors, leading to the "American flag blue" liner peeling away, which Trump had wrongly blamed on vandals.

A spokesperson for El-Sayed's campaign said it raised $2.4 million on Sunday, its largest single-day fundraising haul, fueled by small-dollar donations averaging $36.74 from more than 65,000 donors.

Nonpartisan analysts generally favor Democrats' chances of winning a majority in the House of Representatives.

Winning control of the Senate will be trickier, with those analysts now seeing races in traditionally Republican-leaning states including Texas, Kansas and Iowa as competitive for the opposition party, giving it more options for a path to the majority.

Control of either chamber would constrain Trump's ability to pass legislation and empower Democrats to investigate his administration, while a Senate ?majority would also allow them to block his appointees to federal courts including the Supreme Court.

According to the University of Florida Election Lab, 55 million votes have been cast in person and by mail already, more than the 45 million cast in the 2022 midterm elections.

MICHIGAN RIFT

Stevens called on El-Sayed to condemn an outside group's ad that she said blames Israel for high grocery prices. "That ad was very painful," Stevens told CNN on Sunday night.

"There are so many Democrats who want to vote for our Democratic nominee, and they're just being told, 'Hey, this is a party you don't belong in, or this is a campaign you don't belong in.'"

El-Sayed rejected Stevens' demand, saying she was creating a distraction by revisiting a primary election she lost months prior.

"You guys love to play the condemn game," he told reporters on Saturday when asked about Stevens' demand.

"I've already been clear that that ad was not made by me, and I do not agree with the contents of that ad." El-Sayed, an Egyptian American Muslim born in Michigan, has been targeted by Trump and other Republicans who have repeatedly questioned his loyalty to the US and baselessly called him a terrorist sympathizer whose election would invite attacks on Americans.

El-Sayed has called questions about his loyalty to the US "shameful."

The verbal attacks fit a broader pattern of inflammatory rhetoric from some Republicans targeting Arab Americans, Muslims and transgender people and portraying Democrats as communists and dangerous radicals ahead of the midterms.

Stevens' mother, Maria Marcotte, said her daughter decided to endorse Rogers because of what she described as dangerous political rhetoric from El-Sayed, pointing in part to his past appearances with Hasan Piker, a left-wing streamer who has been criticized for his comments about Israel and American Jews.

"She's really reached a point where she felt like her constituents, the people that she cares about, and the people she knows and loves are scared and frightened by some rhetoric that's coming out," Marcotte said in an interview with Reuters from the porch of her home in Birmingham, a northern Detroit suburb.

Democratic voter Pamela Johnson, 72, criticized Stevens after casting her ballot for El-Sayed in Warren, a Detroit suburb: "Haley Stevens is a traitor."

ALASKA INTERVENTION FALTERS

The Trump administration's attempt to intervene in Alaska's Senate race faltered when a federal judge dismissed the US Justice Department's lawsuit on Sunday that sought to block certification of the results if Republican incumbent Senator Dan S. Sullivan narrowly loses.

The Justice Department argued voters may be confused by the presence of a challenger named Daniel J Sullivan Jr on the same ballot.

The issue has roiled the campaign over the last several days after the New York Times reported that Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign was involved in recruiting the latter Sullivan into the race as a spoiler.

The senator said on Sunday he would accept the results of Tuesday's election even as the Trump administration presses a criminal investigation into the issue.

Peltola has denied involvement, and Sullivan Jr has denied coordinating with Peltola's campaign.

"I think it's great that it got thrown out," said Aileena Bird, a 24-year-old resident of Wasilla, Alaska, who said she voted for Peltola.

"I think that more should be done ?to fight against what Trump has been doing in trying to suppress the voters."

"You guys love to play the condemn game," he told reporters on Saturday when asked about Stevens' demand.

"I've already been clear that that ad was not made by me, and I do not agree with the contents of that ad." El-Sayed, an Egyptian American Muslim born in Michigan, has been targeted by Trump and other Republicans who have repeatedly questioned his loyalty to the US and baselessly called him a terrorist sympathizer whose election would invite attacks on Americans.
El-Sayed has called questions about his loyalty to the US "shameful."

The verbal attacks fit a broader pattern of inflammatory rhetoric from some Republicans targeting Arab Americans, Muslims and transgender people and portraying Democrats as communists and dangerous radicals ahead of the midterms.

Stevens' mother, Maria Marcotte, said her daughter decided to endorse Rogers because of what she described as dangerous political rhetoric from El-Sayed, pointing in part to his past appearances with Hasan Piker, a left-wing streamer who has been criticized for his comments about Israel and American Jews.

"She's really reached a point where she felt like her constituents, the people that she cares about, and the people she knows and loves are scared and frightened by some rhetoric that's coming out," Marcotte said in an interview with Reuters from the porch of her home in Birmingham, a northern Detroit suburb.
Democratic voter Pamela Johnson, 72, criticized Stevens after casting her ballot for El-Sayed in Warren, a Detroit suburb: "Haley Stevens is a traitor."
ALASKA INTERVENTION FALTERS

The Trump administration's attempt to intervene in Alaska's Senate race faltered when a federal judge dismissed the US Justice Department's lawsuit on Sunday that sought to block certification of the results if Republican incumbent Senator Dan S. Sullivan narrowly loses.
The Justice Department argued voters may be confused by the presence of a challenger named Daniel J Sullivan Jr on the same ballot.

The issue has roiled the campaign over the last several days after the New York Times reported that Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign was involved in recruiting the latter Sullivan into the race as a spoiler.
The senator said on Sunday he would accept the results of Tuesday's election even as the Trump administration presses a criminal investigation into the issue.
Peltola has denied involvement, and Sullivan Jr has denied coordinating with Peltola's campaign.
"I think it's great that it got thrown out," said Aileena Bird, a 24-year-old resident of Wasilla, Alaska, who said she voted for Peltola.
"I think that more should be done ?to fight against what Trump has been doing in trying to suppress the voters."

headline: China urges deeper political and institutional exchanges
description: China urges deeper political and institutional exchanges
author: Kamran Yousaf
article_text:
Pakistan's political parties have long supported friendship with China and provided a strong political foundation for bilateral relations, visiting Chinese Communist Party official Liu Haixing said on Monday as he held meetings with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir.

Liu, minister of the International Department of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC), also called for deeper political and institutional exchanges between the two countries.

During his meeting with the prime minister, Shehbaz reaffirmed that Pakistan and China enjoyed an "ironclad, time-tested and All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership," describing the friendship as anchored in mutual trust, respect and deep-rooted bonds between the peoples of the two countries.

According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office, Shehbaz stressed the importance of sustained political engagement and party-to-party exchanges in further strengthening bilateral relations.

He appreciated the role played by the International Department of the CPC in fostering institutional linkages and promoting cooperation between the political leadership of the two countries.

The prime minister reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to working closely with China and commended the shared focus on advancing cooperation in trade, investment, connectivity, infrastructure development, information technology and agricultural modernisation.

Liu conveyed the greetings of the Chinese leadership and reaffirmed Beijing's commitment to further deepening its longstanding friendship with Pakistan. He also appreciated the momentum in high-level and party-to-party exchanges aimed at strengthening bilateral ties.

The two sides exchanged views on regional and international developments and reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining close coordination at bilateral and multilateral forums. Shehbaz also hosted a banquet in honour of the visiting Chinese dignitary and his delegation.

Earlier, Liu called on Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir at the General Headquarters in Rawalpindi.

According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the two discussed evolving regional and international security dynamics, bilateral relations and matters of mutual interest.

Field Marshal Munir highlighted the historic and time-tested relationship between Pakistan and China and emphasised the importance of sustained high-level engagement, stronger institutional linkages and expanded cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

Liu appreciated Pakistan's contributions to regional peace and stability and expressed confidence in further advancing the longstanding strategic partnership. Both sides reiterated their resolve to strengthen the All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership.

The meetings with the prime minister and the country's military leadership were among the most significant engagements of Liu's three-day visit, which comes as Pakistan and China mark 75 years of diplomatic relations.

Symposium in Islamabad

Addressing a high-level symposium in Islamabad on Chinese President Xi Jinping's thought on party-building and governance, Dar said China's experience in institutional discipline, organisational capacity, accountability and people-centred governance offered valuable lessons for Pakistan.

"We acknowledge and commend the intellectual contribution of President Xi Jinping and his thought on party building and the experience of the Communist Party of China in translating his principles into effective governance and tangible development outcomes," Dar said.

He said China's progress had been driven by the CPC's commitment to party discipline, organisational capacity, combating corruption and people-centred governance.

Dar highlighted China's poverty alleviation record, saying sustained policy efforts had lifted hundreds of millions of people out of poverty, making a historic contribution to global poverty reduction.

He said China had achieved its first centenary goal of building a moderately prosperous society and was now advancing towards its second goal of becoming a modern country.

The deputy prime minister said Pakistan could benefit from exchanging governance experiences with China, particularly in leadership development, institutional strengthening, economic management and development planning.

Referring to Pakistan's economic situation, Dar said the country had made significant strides towards economic self-reliance and stabilisation and was now moving towards economic consolidation.

He attributed the progress to governance reforms, including macroeconomic discipline, institutional modernisation, digital tax administration and simplified regulations.

Dar said the 75-year relationship had evolved into an All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership based on mutual trust, mutual respect and mutual support.

He described the broad-based political consensus in Pakistan in support of ties with China as a major strength of the relationship and called it a vital strategic asset. Dar also called for stronger cooperation between political parties, parliaments, universities, think tanks and training institutions.

He said the China-Pakistan Political Parties Forum and the CPEC Political Parties Joint Consultation Mechanism provided important platforms for sustained dialogue, political cooperation and exchanges of experience.

He recalled that Pakistan had proposed five political corridors covering political dialogue, governance cooperation, youth engagement, people-to-people exchanges and regional cooperation.

Dar said political parties and institutions played an important role in building consensus, ensuring policy continuity and facilitating the implementation of bilateral commitments.

He called for strengthening the organisational capacity of political parties, particularly their grassroots structures, while emphasising transparency, accountability, institutional discipline and long-term planning.

He also stressed the importance of parliamentary cooperation between Pakistan's Senate and National Assembly and China's National People's Congress and Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference.

On regional developments, the FM said Pakistan and China had jointly launched a five-point peace initiative for restoring peace in the Middle East during his visit to Beijing on March 31 this year.

He also referred to President Xi's subsequent four-point proposal for the Middle East, describing it as an expression of China's approach towards promoting comprehensive, common and indivisible security.

Dar said China's global initiatives reflected its commitment to fairness, justice and a more equitable international governance system, particularly for developing countries and the Global South.

Senator Sherry Rehman, who also addressed the symposium, highlighted the importance of political parties in the development, progress and prosperity of a country.

PCECC event

Liu's visit also featured the inauguration of the Pakistan-China Research Centre for Party and State Governance.

The event, organised by the Pakistan-China Economic and Cultural Council (PCECC), was attended by Senate Chairman Syed Yousuf Raza Gilani, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and Chinese Ambassador Jiang Zaidong, among others.

Gilani accepted the honourary chairmanship of the newly established research centre, which is intended to provide a platform for research, policy dialogue and practical cooperation between the two countries.

Liu called for closer exchanges among political parties and socio-economic groups in both countries and urged the two sides to implement the consensus reached by their leadership on upgrading the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

Governor Kundi welcomed the Chinese delegation and invited Chinese investors to explore investment opportunities in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Liu's visit is significant because of the institutional role he holds within China's political system.

Unlike conventional diplomatic engagement conducted through China's Foreign Ministry, the International Department of the CPC Central Committee manages relations with political parties and organisations around the world, including ruling and opposition parties.

The department provides a separate channel for political exchanges, governance discussions and institutional cooperation alongside conventional government-to-government diplomacy.

Liu, a member of the 20th CPC Central Committee, was appointed minister of the International Department in September 2025. A career diplomat, he previously served as assistant foreign minister and held senior positions within China's diplomatic and party structures.

His visit also follows a meeting with Dar in Beijing in January, when the two discussed party-to-party exchanges, regional developments and cooperation under CPEC.

The latest engagements underscore the two countries' efforts to expand their relationship beyond traditional diplomatic, economic and defence cooperation to include political parties, parliamentary institutions, think tanks and academic organisations.

The prime minister reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to working closely with China and commended the shared focus on advancing cooperation in trade, investment, connectivity, infrastructure development, information technology and agricultural modernisation.

Liu conveyed the greetings of the Chinese leadership and reaffirmed Beijing's commitment to further deepening its longstanding friendship with Pakistan. He also appreciated the momentum in high-level and party-to-party exchanges aimed at strengthening bilateral ties.

The two sides exchanged views on regional and international developments and reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining close coordination at bilateral and multilateral forums. Shehbaz also hosted a banquet in honour of the visiting Chinese dignitary and his delegation.

Earlier, Liu called on Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir at the General Headquarters in Rawalpindi.

According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the two discussed evolving regional and international security dynamics, bilateral relations and matters of mutual interest.

Field Marshal Munir highlighted the historic and time-tested relationship between Pakistan and China and emphasised the importance of sustained high-level engagement, stronger institutional linkages and expanded cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

Liu appreciated Pakistan's contributions to regional peace and stability and expressed confidence in further advancing the longstanding strategic partnership. Both sides reiterated their resolve to strengthen the All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership.

The meetings with the prime minister and the country's military leadership were among the most significant engagements of Liu's three-day visit, which comes as Pakistan and China mark 75 years of diplomatic relations.

Symposium in Islamabad

Addressing a high-level symposium in Islamabad on Chinese President Xi Jinping's thought on party-building and governance, Dar said China's experience in institutional discipline, organisational capacity, accountability and people-centred governance offered valuable lessons for Pakistan.

"We acknowledge and commend the intellectual contribution of President Xi Jinping and his thought on party building and the experience of the Communist Party of China in translating his principles into effective governance and tangible development outcomes," Dar said.

He said China's progress had been driven by the CPC's commitment to party discipline, organisational capacity, combating corruption and people-centred governance.

Dar highlighted China's poverty alleviation record, saying sustained policy efforts had lifted hundreds of millions of people out of poverty, making a historic contribution to global poverty reduction.

He said China had achieved its first centenary goal of building a moderately prosperous society and was now advancing towards its second goal of becoming a modern country.

The deputy prime minister said Pakistan could benefit from exchanging governance experiences with China, particularly in leadership development, institutional strengthening, economic management and development planning.

Referring to Pakistan's economic situation, Dar said the country had made significant strides towards economic self-reliance and stabilisation and was now moving towards economic consolidation.

He attributed the progress to governance reforms, including macroeconomic discipline, institutional modernisation, digital tax administration and simplified regulations.

Dar said the 75-year relationship had evolved into an All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership based on mutual trust, mutual respect and mutual support.

He described the broad-based political consensus in Pakistan in support of ties with China as a major strength of the relationship and called it a vital strategic asset. Dar also called for stronger cooperation between political parties, parliaments, universities, think tanks and training institutions.

He said the China-Pakistan Political Parties Forum and the CPEC Political Parties Joint Consultation Mechanism provided important platforms for sustained dialogue, political cooperation and exchanges of experience.

He recalled that Pakistan had proposed five political corridors covering political dialogue, governance cooperation, youth engagement, people-to-people exchanges and regional cooperation.

Dar said political parties and institutions played an important role in building consensus, ensuring policy continuity and facilitating the implementation of bilateral commitments.

He called for strengthening the organisational capacity of political parties, particularly their grassroots structures, while emphasising transparency, accountability, institutional discipline and long-term planning.

He also stressed the importance of parliamentary cooperation between Pakistan's Senate and National Assembly and China's National People's Congress and Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference.

On regional developments, the FM said Pakistan and China had jointly launched a five-point peace initiative for restoring peace in the Middle East during his visit to Beijing on March 31 this year.

He also referred to President Xi's subsequent four-point proposal for the Middle East, describing it as an expression of China's approach towards promoting comprehensive, common and indivisible security.

Dar said China's global initiatives reflected its commitment to fairness, justice and a more equitable international governance system, particularly for developing countries and the Global South.

Senator Sherry Rehman, who also addressed the symposium, highlighted the importance of political parties in the development, progress and prosperity of a country.

PCECC event

Liu's visit also featured the inauguration of the Pakistan-China Research Centre for Party and State Governance.

The event, organised by the Pakistan-China Economic and Cultural Council (PCECC), was attended by Senate Chairman Syed Yousuf Raza Gilani, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and Chinese Ambassador Jiang Zaidong, among others.

Gilani accepted the honourary chairmanship of the newly established research centre, which is intended to provide a platform for research, policy dialogue and practical cooperation between the two countries.

Liu called for closer exchanges among political parties and socio-economic groups in both countries and urged the two sides to implement the consensus reached by their leadership on upgrading the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

Governor Kundi welcomed the Chinese delegation and invited Chinese investors to explore investment opportunities in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Liu's visit is significant because of the institutional role he holds within China's political system.

Unlike conventional diplomatic engagement conducted through China's Foreign Ministry, the International Department of the CPC Central Committee manages relations with political parties and organisations around the world, including ruling and opposition parties.

The department provides a separate channel for political exchanges, governance discussions and institutional cooperation alongside conventional government-to-government diplomacy.

Liu, a member of the 20th CPC Central Committee, was appointed minister of the International Department in September 2025. A career diplomat, he previously served as assistant foreign minister and held senior positions within China's diplomatic and party structures.

His visit also follows a meeting with Dar in Beijing in January, when the two discussed party-to-party exchanges, regional developments and cooperation under CPEC.

The latest engagements underscore the two countries' efforts to expand their relationship beyond traditional diplomatic, economic and defence cooperation to include political parties, parliamentary institutions, think tanks and academic organisations.

headline: Iran says talks continue despite no breakthrough
description: Iran says talks continue despite no breakthrough
author: agencies
article_text:
Contacts between Iran and the United States to end their eight-month war are continuing, Tehran said on Monday, after days of ?Iranian talks with Qatari mediators ended with altered proposals but no breakthrough.

"Consultations through mediators are very intensive. We have presented our conditions and proposals and everything depends on the political rationality of Washington," Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said in comments carried by ?state media outlet IRNA.

Amid fears the conflict could reignite after Tuesday's midterm elections in the United States, China and Russia both spoke out on Monday against the possibility of renewed military action in a war that has hit the ?global economy.

While oil prices fell nearly 4% on Monday on hopes that the latest round of mediation could lead to a diplomatic solution to the crisis, Iranian sources said they believed a new US attack was still more likely than a deal.

Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said the plan Iran had submitted in September to end the war remained the focus of discussions, but he confirmed comments attributed to Araqchi on Saturday that the ?proposal could be shortened.

"The basis of dialogue and talks between Iran and the US via mediators is still Iran's seven-step proposal, which is now condensed, making it possible to implement it within two days," he said.

US President Donald Trump rejected the seven-step proposal in September.

The plan would call for the US to end its blockade on Iranian ports, Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz waterway, a US waiver on Iranian oil sales, the cancellation of new sanctions on Iran and then talks on other issues.

Baghaei reiterated that ?condensing the plan would not change Iran's underlying stance that a return to talks on the country's nuclear programme could only happen after it verified that all its conditions were met.

Asked whether the possibility of transferring Iran's highly enriched uranium stockpile to another country was raised in the talks, and whether Iran might agree to that, he said no.

An official briefed on the talks said Iran's negotiators had left on Sunday but not because of any problems in the talks, and added that a draft proposal was being circulated without elaborating.

RUSSIAN AND CHINESE CONCERNS

The war, which the US and Israel launched suddenly on February 28, has led to Iran's closure of the key Strait of Hormuz waterway, the US blockade on Iranian ports, repeated bouts of Iranian drone and missile fire on Gulf states and renewed conflict in Yemen.

Trump has repeatedly said there would be no new attack on Iran before Tuesday's midterm elections. Iran has said it will respond to any resumed attack aggressively with plans to strike targets both within and outside the Middle East.

China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Monday that all parties to the conflict should focus on political solutions rather than resorting to arms again, after a meeting with senior Iranian security official Ali Bagheri Kani in Beijing.

China, a major customer for Gulf energy products, is engaging more actively in Middle East diplomacy this week, hosting Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq al-Said, whose country flanks the southern side of the Strait of Hormuz.

Wang also met Saudi Arabia's national security advisor Musaed bin Mohammed al-Aiban in Beijing on Monday, China's Foreign Ministry said, adding that all sides should work to safeguard regional energy and shipping lane security.

In Moscow, the Russian Foreign Ministry said reports of new military action against Iran were a cause for extreme concern and called for increased diplomatic efforts.

Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke by phone with Iran's top security official Mohsen Rezaei on Monday, Iranian state media reported.

Underscoring the risks to global energy supply, a Qatari liquefied natural gas (LNG) tanker was struck in the Gulf by unidentified objects on Friday, its operator Nakilat said on Sunday.

While attacks on oil tankers in the Gulf and Red Sea have been common during the conflict, attacks on LNG carriers have been rare, with the last reported incident with a ?Qatari tanker happening in early July.

Trump could launch nuclear strike

US commentator Tucker Carlson claimed late Sunday that the Trump administration could be days away from launching a nuclear strike on Iran, alleging that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressuring President Donald Trump to authorize an attack on a suspected nuclear site in central Iran.

In a lengthy post on the US social media company X, Carlson identified the potential target as Pickaxe Mountain, where Israeli intelligence allegedly believes Iran has resumed its nuclear enrichment program.

Carlson is a conservative political commentator and former Fox News host whose program, Tucker Carlson Tonight, aired from 2016 to 2023.

He now hosts an independent political show on X, where he regularly comments on US foreign policy and international affairs.

Carlson claimed conventional US weapons could not penetrate the estimated 300 feet of solid granite protecting underground tunnels at the site, leaving a nuclear strike as the only military option.

"Bibi (Netanyahu) calls Trump about it every day," Carlson quoted an unnamed informed observer as saying.

Carlson argued that Netanyahu's political survival is driving his push for further military action. He claimed Netanyahu needs Trump's intervention to secure a 61-seat majority in the Knesset following the latest election results, warning that otherwise he could lose power and face investigations and possible imprisonment.

He also alleged that Netanyahu has been pressing senior US officials, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and US Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper, to resume major combat operations.

Carlson also claimed that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA Director John Ratcliffe were following Netanyahu's lead.

He further said former President Barack Obama had also opposed the Iran peace agreement being drafted in Doha.

Fears of regional escalation

Carlson said US allies in the Middle East were increasingly concerned about renewed fighting. He claimed Netanyahu secretly traveled to Abu Dhabi on Sept 27 to persuade the UAE to support a final attack on Iran, but Emirati officials refused.

Warning of the economic consequences, Carlson said eight months of conflict had severely affected Gulf economies, as well as global energy and fertilizer markets. He claimed 11 of the world's approximately 850 oil supertankers were badly damaged in the Strait of Hormuz in October alone.

He also warned that a nuclear explosion at Pickaxe Mountain could contaminate the Gulf and threaten the water supply of around 100 million people.

Carlson argued that a US nuclear strike could establish a dangerous precedent, potentially encouraging Russia to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine, triggering renewed nuclear tensions between India and Pakistan, and prompting North Korea to attack Seoul.

"After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final," he wrote.

He further alleged that the Trump administration had quietly revised US nuclear doctrine since February to make the first use of so-called "battlefield nukes" easier and more likely.

Vance, Witkoff urge Trump to pursue diplomacy

Carlson said Trump could decide by Nov 7 whether to authorize the use of nuclear weapons, adding that Vice President JD Vance and special envoy Steve Witkoff were urging him to pursue a diplomatic agreement with Tehran.

Although acknowledging that negotiations would be difficult, Carlson said people who had spoken with Iranian decision-makers believed there was a consensus that further conflict would benefit no one and that an agreement was worth pursuing.

He concluded by warning that the consequences of a nuclear strike would extend far beyond Iran, arguing that the international public had been excluded from decisions that could threaten millions of lives.

"Now would be the time for them to speak up," Carlson wrote.

US could hit Iran's remaining nuclear sites 'in 10 minutes'

Carlson's claims follow Trump's remarks to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Saturday that one or two Iranian nuclear facilities remained potential targets and that the US could strike them within 10 minutes.

Trump specifically mentioned Pickaxe Mountain, saying he had military plans for the area, but did not indicate that a nuclear strike had been authorized.

"You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly," he added.

In an Oct 16 interview with Newsmax, he explicitly ruled out using nuclear weapons against Iran.

DUBAI/ISTANBUL:

Contacts between Iran and the United States to end their eight-month war are continuing, Tehran said on Monday, after days of ?Iranian talks with Qatari mediators ended with altered proposals but no breakthrough.

"Consultations through mediators are very intensive. We have presented our conditions and proposals and everything depends on the political rationality of Washington," Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said in comments carried by ?state media outlet IRNA.

Amid fears the conflict could reignite after Tuesday's midterm elections in the United States, China and Russia both spoke out on Monday against the possibility of renewed military action in a war that has hit the ?global economy.

While oil prices fell nearly 4% on Monday on hopes that the latest round of mediation could lead to a diplomatic solution to the crisis, Iranian sources said they believed a new US attack was still more likely than a deal.

Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said the plan Iran had submitted in September to end the war remained the focus of discussions, but he confirmed comments attributed to Araqchi on Saturday that the ?proposal could be shortened.

"The basis of dialogue and talks between Iran and the US via mediators is still Iran's seven-step proposal, which is now condensed, making it possible to implement it within two days," he said.

US President Donald Trump rejected the seven-step proposal in September.

The plan would call for the US to end its blockade on Iranian ports, Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz waterway, a US waiver on Iranian oil sales, the cancellation of new sanctions on Iran and then talks on other issues.

Baghaei reiterated that ?condensing the plan would not change Iran's underlying stance that a return to talks on the country's nuclear programme could only happen after it verified that all its conditions were met.

Asked whether the possibility of transferring Iran's highly enriched uranium stockpile to another country was raised in the talks, and whether Iran might agree to that, he said no.

An official briefed on the talks said Iran's negotiators had left on Sunday but not because of any problems in the talks, and added that a draft proposal was being circulated without elaborating.

RUSSIAN AND CHINESE CONCERNS

The war, which the US and Israel launched suddenly on February 28, has led to Iran's closure of the key Strait of Hormuz waterway, the US blockade on Iranian ports, repeated bouts of Iranian drone and missile fire on Gulf states and renewed conflict in Yemen.

Trump has repeatedly said there would be no new attack on Iran before Tuesday's midterm elections. Iran has said it will respond to any resumed attack aggressively with plans to strike targets both within and outside the Middle East.

China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Monday that all parties to the conflict should focus on political solutions rather than resorting to arms again, after a meeting with senior Iranian security official Ali Bagheri Kani in Beijing.

China, a major customer for Gulf energy products, is engaging more actively in Middle East diplomacy this week, hosting Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq al-Said, whose country flanks the southern side of the Strait of Hormuz.

Wang also met Saudi Arabia's national security advisor Musaed bin Mohammed al-Aiban in Beijing on Monday, China's Foreign Ministry said, adding that all sides should work to safeguard regional energy and shipping lane security.

In Moscow, the Russian Foreign Ministry said reports of new military action against Iran were a cause for extreme concern and called for increased diplomatic efforts.

Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke by phone with Iran's top security official Mohsen Rezaei on Monday, Iranian state media reported.

Underscoring the risks to global energy supply, a Qatari liquefied natural gas (LNG) tanker was struck in the Gulf by unidentified objects on Friday, its operator Nakilat said on Sunday.

While attacks on oil tankers in the Gulf and Red Sea have been common during the conflict, attacks on LNG carriers have been rare, with the last reported incident with a ?Qatari tanker happening in early July.

Trump could launch nuclear strike

US commentator Tucker Carlson claimed late Sunday that the Trump administration could be days away from launching a nuclear strike on Iran, alleging that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressuring President Donald Trump to authorize an attack on a suspected nuclear site in central Iran.

In a lengthy post on the US social media company X, Carlson identified the potential target as Pickaxe Mountain, where Israeli intelligence allegedly believes Iran has resumed its nuclear enrichment program.

Carlson is a conservative political commentator and former Fox News host whose program, Tucker Carlson Tonight, aired from 2016 to 2023.

He now hosts an independent political show on X, where he regularly comments on US foreign policy and international affairs.

Carlson claimed conventional US weapons could not penetrate the estimated 300 feet of solid granite protecting underground tunnels at the site, leaving a nuclear strike as the only military option.

"Bibi (Netanyahu) calls Trump about it every day," Carlson quoted an unnamed informed observer as saying.

Carlson argued that Netanyahu's political survival is driving his push for further military action. He claimed Netanyahu needs Trump's intervention to secure a 61-seat majority in the Knesset following the latest election results, warning that otherwise he could lose power and face investigations and possible imprisonment.

He also alleged that Netanyahu has been pressing senior US officials, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and US Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper, to resume major combat operations.

Carlson also claimed that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA Director John Ratcliffe were following Netanyahu's lead.

He further said former President Barack Obama had also opposed the Iran peace agreement being drafted in Doha.

Fears of regional escalation

Carlson said US allies in the Middle East were increasingly concerned about renewed fighting. He claimed Netanyahu secretly traveled to Abu Dhabi on Sept 27 to persuade the UAE to support a final attack on Iran, but Emirati officials refused.

Warning of the economic consequences, Carlson said eight months of conflict had severely affected Gulf economies, as well as global energy and fertilizer markets. He claimed 11 of the world's approximately 850 oil supertankers were badly damaged in the Strait of Hormuz in October alone.

He also warned that a nuclear explosion at Pickaxe Mountain could contaminate the Gulf and threaten the water supply of around 100 million people.

Carlson argued that a US nuclear strike could establish a dangerous precedent, potentially encouraging Russia to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine, triggering renewed nuclear tensions between India and Pakistan, and prompting North Korea to attack Seoul.

"After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final," he wrote.

He further alleged that the Trump administration had quietly revised US nuclear doctrine since February to make the first use of so-called "battlefield nukes" easier and more likely.

Vance, Witkoff urge Trump to pursue diplomacy

Carlson said Trump could decide by Nov 7 whether to authorize the use of nuclear weapons, adding that Vice President JD Vance and special envoy Steve Witkoff were urging him to pursue a diplomatic agreement with Tehran.

Although acknowledging that negotiations would be difficult, Carlson said people who had spoken with Iranian decision-makers believed there was a consensus that further conflict would benefit no one and that an agreement was worth pursuing.

He concluded by warning that the consequences of a nuclear strike would extend far beyond Iran, arguing that the international public had been excluded from decisions that could threaten millions of lives.

"Now would be the time for them to speak up," Carlson wrote.

US could hit Iran's remaining nuclear sites 'in 10 minutes'

Carlson's claims follow Trump's remarks to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Saturday that one or two Iranian nuclear facilities remained potential targets and that the US could strike them within 10 minutes.

Trump specifically mentioned Pickaxe Mountain, saying he had military plans for the area, but did not indicate that a nuclear strike had been authorized.

"You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly," he added.

In an Oct 16 interview with Newsmax, he explicitly ruled out using nuclear weapons against Iran.

headline: Hackers shut down shop fridges across Europe
description: Hackers shut down shop fridges across Europe
author: Reuters
article_text:
A hacking attack on European supermarkets spread across the continent on Monday, hitting fridges and freezers from Sweden to Belgium and forcing stores to throw away food in an incident that echoed a similar attack in France last month.

The attack, which raised temperatures in refrigerator and freezer units at dozens of stores, hit supermarket groups Ahold Delhaize and Colruyt in Belgium and Luxembourg, as well as Swedish grocers ICA and Coop. Furniture-to-meatballs retailer IKEA also saw at least one store affected.

"Everything is destroyed," Engla Ingwall, sales manager at an ICA franchise store in Stockholm, told Reuters during a visit to the store on Monday, adding the attack occurred at 2 a.m. (0100 GMT) but was only noticed hours later.

"There has been a cyberattack and all our freezers reached 50 degrees (Celsius)."

A spokesperson for privately held ICA said the company was aware that a "limited number of stores were affected by an incident overnight, which impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems".

The latest incidents follow an attack in France last month when police said hackers seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets, causing fires and food losses. Ahold also reported a cybersecurity incident to police last month.

While no one has claimed responsibility for either attack, the incidents have heightened concerns among European authorities about hybrid threats to infrastructure amid growing security tensions since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

headline: Nine killed in Florida business jet crash
description: Nine killed in Florida business jet crash
author: Reuters
article_text:
A Learjet crashed on Sunday afternoon in a residential area in Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people on board, US transportation officials said.

The private jet had taken off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, the Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement.

"It was a big-time tragedy that happened," Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said at a press conference near the crash site in Lake Worth Beach. "When you see that video, it's a jarring thing. It was like a missile coming down, and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere."

The National Transportation Safety Board said it had launched an investigation into the crash, which Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called a "horrific tragedy."

The crash left a "massive crater" by the road near the entrance to a mobile home park, Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores said at the news conference. About 600 people were being evacuated from the area and relocated to two shelters in the county, Flores said.

Heavy rainfall and thunderstorms were occurring in the area at the time, forecaster AccuWeather said in a statement.

An audio recording from a Miami air traffic control center posted on LiveATC, a site that broadcasts air traffic control communications, captured the plane's final moments before the crash in unusual detail.

At first, someone in the plane's cockpit reported to an air traffic controller that they were "managing the ice" but faced "moderate" turbulence and were seeking "better rides".

Less than a minute later, the person said "Mayday, mayday," reporting that the plane was suddenly descending at a rate of 10,000 feet per minute.

Seconds later, the person said they were declaring an emergency, with the rate of descent accelerating to 20,000 feet per minute.

Less than 20 seconds later, the person said: "We're going to crash into the ground" before saying that the descent rate had reached 22,000 feet per minute as the plane started banking.

About 35 seconds after the initial mayday announcement, the last thing heard from the cockpit was a rapidly spoken "We're out of time."

Flight tracking website Flightradar24 said data showed the vertical descent rate at one point exceeded 32,000 feet per minute.

headline: Spain deports asylum seekers
description: Spain deports asylum seekers
author: Reuters
article_text:
Spain has returned to Morocco more than a dozen sub-Saharan African and Asian migrants who reached the Spanish enclave of Ceuta and were turned down for asylum, the first deportation of its kind from the enclave since a mass border crossing in July.

The Interior Ministry said the group had been sent back to Morocco after it agreed to receive them and they remained on Moroccan territory at present. It declined to give numbers or nationalities but migrant and rights charities operating in Ceuta said 16 people from Senegal, Nigeria, Yemen, Cameroon and Bangladesh were deported.

The NGOs claim such returns fail to take into account the risks associated with Morocco's treatment of migrants from other countries and fly in the face of the values espoused by Spain's leftist government.

Virginia Alvarez, an Amnesty International researcher, said Spain's posture was hypocritical.

"Spain, despite its (progressive) speeches in Europe, is not ensuring that human rights guarantees are met for people who cross its borders in Ceuta and Melilla," she said. "Morocco does not respect many human rights."

Morocco's Interior Ministry did not respond to Reuters requests for comment.

headline: Xi calls for lasting peace in Middle East
description: Xi calls for lasting peace in Middle East
author: agencies
article_text:
The Middle East and Gulf region should not become a battleground for great-power rivalry and China is willing to work with Arab nations to achieve lasting peace, Chinese President Xi Jinping told Oman's sultan on Monday.

Xi told Omani Sultan Haitham bin Tariq al-Said that the world is undergoing profound changes.

"The Middle East Gulf region should not become an arena for great-power rivalry and geopolitical conflict. Peace and stability in the region require joint nurturing and protection by all parties," Xi said, according to China's Foreign Ministry.

China has consistently been committed to stopping the war, and hopes to contribute "wisdom and solutions to resolving the region's security dilemmas," he added.

China is willing to strengthen communication and coordination with Arab countries, including the Gulf Cooperation Council states, to work together toward restoring peace and achieving lasting stability and security, Xi said.

In a 20-point joint statement, both sides said they agree that normal and safe navigation should resume in the Strait of Hormuz. The countries also called for the US and Iran to pursue peaceful options, return to the agreement struck in June aimed at ending the conflict and restart dialogue.

China's Foreign Ministry said later on Monday that Zhai Jun, its special envoy to the Middle East, would visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia this month.

Haitham arrived in Beijing on Sunday for a two-day visit, the first by an Omani head of state since the countries established ties in 1978.

Haitham told Xi his government had deep appreciation for China's positions on key issues concerning the region, Omani state media reported.

"We believe that development

and stability are inextricably linked," he said.

"The prosperity of nations requires an environment defined by security, peace, respect for state sovereignty, and adherence to international law - an environment where disputes are resolved through peaceful means."

He also said Oman was open to entering into a preferential bilateral trade and investment agreement with China.

headline: Russian bombing kills 24 in Ukraine
description: Russian bombing kills 24 in Ukraine
author: Reuters
article_text:
.

Russian forces bombed a school in a village in Ukraine's southeastern Zaporizhzhia region on Monday, killing 24 people, Ukraine's emergency services said.

The emergency services said two members of a rescue crew were among the dead in the village of Komyshuvakha.

President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, writing on Telegram, said Russian forces initially dropped aerial bombs on a school in the village, used for distributing humanitarian assistance.

"After the first air strike, there was a repeat strike with nine more bombs, directly on the shelter where people were gathered," Zelenskiy wrote.

"The Russians could not have been unaware that every week residents who have remained in Komyshuvakha were receiving assistance right there. This is yet further proof that Russia does not want any kind of de-escalation, any real justice."
