headline: Pakistan, Saudi agree to enhance cooperation in media, culture, tourism
description: Tarar stresses need for joint initiatives to promote cultural cooperation introduce Pakistani TV dramas in Riyadh
author: APP
article_text:
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and Saudi Ambassador to Pakistan Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy on Tuesday agreed to further strengthen cooperation between the two brotherly countries in the fields of information, broadcasting, media, culture, and public relations.

During a meeting with the Saudi ambassador, the minister welcomed him to Pakistan and congratulated him on his diplomatic assignment, expressing confidence that his tenure would further strengthen the longstanding ties between the two countries.

The minister said Pakistan-Saudi Arabia relations were reaching new heights, with vast opportunities for expanding cooperation in media, culture, drama, music, tourism, and people-to-people contacts.

He said the relationship between the two countries spanned generations and was rooted not merely in diplomatic and political engagement but also in shared history, religious bonds and strong public connections.

Referring to the strategic partnership between the two countries, the minister said the defence agreement reflected the strength of their cooperation in the defence sector.

He observed that under the dynamic leadership of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Saudi Arabia had undergone remarkable transformation in economic and cultural spheres. The promotion of tourism in AlUla and the modern presentation of the historical and cultural significance of Diriyah were prominent examples of the Saudi leadership’s vision, he added.

Emphasising the importance of cultural diplomacy, Tarar stressed the need for joint initiatives to promote cultural cooperation and introduce Pakistani television dramas in Saudi Arabia.

He said Pakistani dramas reflected family values, eastern traditions and Islamic culture and could serve as an effective medium for bringing the people of the two countries closer.

The minister also proposed exchanges of delegations comprising writers, poets, artists, musicians, media professionals and digital content creators to strengthen cultural and professional linkages.

Highlighting Pakistan’s tourism potential, he invited Saudi media representatives, tourists and digital influencers to visit the country’s diverse tourist destinations and explore its natural beauty and historical heritage.

Recalling the sacrifice of Pakistani national Farman Ali Khan, who lost his life while saving several people during the 2009 floods in Jeddah, the minister said his act of bravery represented the enduring bonds of love, solidarity and brotherhood between the people of Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.

The minister also emphasised cooperation to counter misinformation and negative propaganda, strengthen fact-checking mechanisms and develop content reflecting the shared cultural values of the two countries.

He proposed the establishment of a joint working group comprising focal persons and technical teams from both sides to pursue practical cooperation in these areas.

Briefing the Saudi ambassador on Pakistan’s use of social media influencers for public awareness and the promotion of key government initiatives, Tarar said a social media post regarding the prime minister’s fuel relief scheme had received more than eight million views.

The Saudi ambassador described the strong brotherly relations between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, based on mutual trust, respect and political and military cooperation, as a matter of pride.

He emphasised the need to further expand collaboration between the two countries in cultural events, arts, literature and media.

He proposed the establishment of a joint working group comprising focal persons and technical teams from both sides to pursue practical cooperation in these areas.

The Saudi ambassador described the strong brotherly relations between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, based on mutual trust, respect and political and military cooperation, as a matter of pride.

He emphasised the need to further expand collaboration between the two countries in cultural events, arts, literature and media.

headline: Mckenna Grace says she avoids hypersexual roles in hopes of playing Disney princess one day
description: Mckenna Grace says she avoids roles involving nudity, citing her ambition to become Disney princess
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Mckenna Grace has revealed that she turns down acting roles involving nudity or highly sexualised scenes, explaining that she hopes to one day play a Disney princess.

Speaking to Cosmopolitan during the press tour for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, the actor discussed whether there were any roles she would refuse.

"At this point, I definitely don't do nudity or very hypersexual things," Grace said. "I respect anybody who can, but it's terrifying to me. I don't know if that'll ever change. It's not like I only do wholesome things — my character literally gets gutted by Ghostface in 'Scream' — but my dream is to try and be a Disney princess someday."

Her comments recall Amy Adams' experience following her portrayal of Giselle in Disney's 2007 film Enchanted. Adams reportedly turned down a risqué Saturday Night Live sketch because she was concerned about how it might affect the character's image among younger fans.

Andy Samberg previously discussed the proposed sketch on The Lonely Island and Seth Meyers podcast, explaining that Adams declined because children who loved Enchanted might encounter the material.

"She was like, 'That's really funny. I can't do that,'" Samberg recalled. "'Little girls are so obsessed with 'Enchanted' right now. They will find this, and it will be scarring for them. I just can't mix that right now.'"

Grace most recently appeared in Scream 7 and is set to portray Maysilee Donner in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, which arrives in cinemas on November 20. She is also starring as Daphne in Netflix's live-action Scooby-Doo reboot series.

headline: Pakistan-India World Cup clash draws 8.4 million ticket requests
description: More than 120 million ticket applications pour in for the 2027 tournament across three host nations
author: REUTERS
article_text:
More than 120 million ticket applications pour in for the 2027 tournament across three host nations

Nearly 8.4 million ticket applications have been received for India and Pakistan's group-stage clash at next year's Men's ⁠Cricket World Cup, organisers said on Monday. The rivals are set to clash in Johannesburg at ⁠The Wanderers on October 10, 2027. The final, hosted at the same 34,000-seat venue, ⁠trails close ⁠behind with almost eight million ticket requests. Nearly three million fans from 193 countries have applied for tickets in the ballot ⁠window, which remains open ⁠until November 21, for the tournament co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. More than 120 million total ticket ⁠requests have been received for the 14-team showcase that runs October 2 to November 21.

headline: Ben Wang in talks to play Iceman in Marvel’s upcoming ‘X-Men’ film
description: Wang would join a cast featuring Kit Connor, Sadie Sink and Christopher Abbott
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Ben Wang is reportedly in talks to play Iceman in Marvel Studios’ upcoming X-Men film, according to sources cited by Deadline. The casting has not been officially confirmed by Marvel, and negotiations are understood to be ongoing.

The actor, who is also set to appear in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, is being considered for the role of Bobby Drake, one of the original members of the X-Men. The character first appeared in Marvel Comics’ The X-Men No. 1 in September 1963 and is known for his ability to generate and control ice.

If the deal goes through, Wang will join an expanding ensemble that includes Christopher Abbott as Professor X, Adam Driver as Mr Sinister, Kit Connor as Cyclops, Samara Weaving as Emma Frost, Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Maya Boyd as Storm, Asa Germann as Angel and Sadie Sink as Jean Grey.

Other actors reportedly tested for the Iceman role, including Gabriel LaBelle, Jackson Kelly and Rhenzy Feliz. However, their involvement has not been confirmed.

Iceman previously appeared in the 2000s X-Men film series, with Shawn Ashmore portraying the mutant across several instalments.

Jake Schreier is directing the new film from a screenplay by Lee Sung Jin and Joanna Calo. Kevin Feige is producing the project, which is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on May 5, 2028.

Wang has built a growing profile through roles in Karate Kid: Legends, Disney+ series American Born Chinese and Chang Can Dunk. His recent credits also include The Long Walk, directed by Francis Lawrence, and the 2024 Mean Girls film.

The actor is among several performers gaining attention through major studio projects, although Marvel has yet to announce his casting as Iceman officially.

headline: Vivienne Jolie becomes fourth child to drop Brad Pitt's surname after court approval
description: Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt daughter Vivienne's surname change approved by California judge following her siblings
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Vivienne, the 18-year-old daughter of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt, has officially removed her father's surname, becoming the fourth of the former couple's six children to legally adopt the Jolie name.

According to court documents obtained by PEOPLE, a California judge approved Vivienne's name change on Monday, November 2, without objections. She will now be known as Vivienne Marcheline Jolie rather than Vivienne Marcheline Jolie-Pitt.

She initially petitioned to remove Pitt from her surname in July, shortly after turning 18.

Vivienne had previously used the name Jolie professionally. In May 2024, she was credited as Vivienne Jolie in the Playbill for Broadway production The Outsiders, which she helped produce alongside her mother.

Her siblings Maddox, Zahara and Shiloh have also legally dropped Pitt from their surnames. Maddox's name change to Maddox Chivan Jolie became official on September 14, while Zahara's petition to become Zahara Marley Jolie was approved on September 28. Shiloh filed to remove her father's surname on her 18th birthday in 2024.

Jolie and Pitt share six children: Maddox, 25, Pax, 22, Zahara, 21, Shiloh, 20, and twins Vivienne and Knox, 18. The actors separated in 2016 after 12 years together and two years of marriage, finalising their divorce in December 2024.

The children's surname changes come amid reports of limited communication between Pitt and his older children. A source previously told PEOPLE in September that "there's very little communication right now", describing the situation as "a tragedy".

Vivienne and her twin brother Knox were born in July 2008 and are the youngest of the six siblings.

Vivienne, the 18-year-old daughter of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt, has officially removed her father's surname, becoming the fourth of the former couple's six children to legally adopt the Jolie name.

According to court documents obtained by PEOPLE, a California judge approved Vivienne's name change on Monday, November 2, without objections. She will now be known as Vivienne Marcheline Jolie rather than Vivienne Marcheline Jolie-Pitt.

She initially petitioned to remove Pitt from her surname in July, shortly after turning 18.

Vivienne had previously used the name Jolie professionally. In May 2024, she was credited as Vivienne Jolie in the Playbill for Broadway production The Outsiders, which she helped produce alongside her mother.

Her siblings Maddox, Zahara and Shiloh have also legally dropped Pitt from their surnames. The children's surname changes come amid reports of limited communication between Pitt and his older children. A source previously told PEOPLE in September that "there's very little communication right now", describing the situation as "a tragedy".

Vivienne and her twin brother Knox were born in July 2008 and are the youngest of the six siblings.

headline: Whitney Peak felt 'way in over my head' joining 'The Hunger Games' franchise
description: Whitney Peak discusses pressure of joining 'The Hunger Games' alongside co-stars Maya Hawke and Mckenna Grace
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Whitney Peak has opened up about the pressure of joining The Hunger Games franchise, admitting she initially felt overwhelmed by the responsibility of playing a character important to its established story.

The actor features alongside co-stars Maya Hawke and Mckenna Grace on separate digital covers for Cosmopolitan's Winter Issues. The three are preparing to appear in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, which arrives in cinemas on November 20.

Peak, who portrays Lenore Dove Baird in the upcoming film, told the magazine that joining a franchise with such a devoted following was an intimidating experience.

"I was really freaked out….I don't mean to be self-effacing or self-deprecating," she admitted. "I'm just being completely honest that I felt way in over my head with this. When something just feels so much larger than anything you could have conceived and it's something people love, with a character who is really important to the story, and it's just little old me doing all of that…I had to not think about it and just do it."

She also offered a brief hint about the film's emotional impact, telling audiences: "Bring a box of tissues."

Mckenna Grace, who plays Maysilee Donner, also discussed her connection to the franchise. The actor revealed that she was a fan of the films before joining the cast and had even created fan edits.

She jokingly described herself as a "CapCut warrior" after her previous Team Peeta edit, featuring Josh Hutcherson's character, came to light.

Meanwhile, Maya Hawke, who portrays Wiress, said having fellow actors share the experience helped make the pressure more manageable.

"We are all in it together and will sink or swim as a team," she told Cosmopolitan.

headline: Bill Hader to guest star on Quinta Brunson’s ‘Abbott Elementary’
description: The announcement came as Hader promoted his upcoming animated film ‘The Cat in the Hat’
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Bill Hader is set to make a guest appearance on Abbott Elementary, bringing the comedian together with Quinta Brunson for another collaboration.

Hader revealed the news during an appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live, where he was promoting his upcoming animated film The Cat in the Hat. Brunson and Hader both lend their voices to the project, which is scheduled to open in cinemas on November 6.

Details surrounding Hader’s appearance on Abbott Elementary remain under wraps. His character and the episode’s air date have not yet been announced, leaving fans waiting to learn how he will fit into the popular comedy series.

The ABC sitcom, created by Brunson, follows teachers working at an underfunded Philadelphia public school. Since its debut, the series has earned critical acclaim and multiple awards for its ensemble and workplace comedy.

Hader is best known for creating, writing, directing, executive producing and starring in HBO’s Barry, which ran from 2018 to 2023. His performance earned him two Emmy Awards for outstanding lead actor in a comedy series.

He also spent eight seasons on Saturday Night Live from 2005 to 2013 and co-created the comedy series Documentary Now!.

His film credits include The Skeleton Twins, Trainwreck and It Chapter Two. Hader has also built an extensive voice acting career, appearing in animated films such as Inside Out, Finding Dory, Toy Story 4 and the Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs franchise.

The guest appearance marks another television collaboration for Hader, who previously appeared in an episode of Curb Your Enthusiasm in 2021.

Abbott Elementary airs on ABC on Wednesdays at 8.30pm, with episodes available to stream on Hulu the following day. Further details about Hader’s appearance are expected to emerge closer to its broadcast.

headline: US approves Qatar-presented draft deal with Iran: sources
description: It said there had been developments in talks with both sides and that efforts to narrow gaps were continuing
author: Reuters
article_text:
The United States approved a draft memorandum of understanding that Qatari mediators presented to Iran a day ago, sources familiar with the matter said on Tuesday.

“The mediation team briefed Saudi Arabia and the UAE on the memorandum, which they also approved,” the sources told Qatari newspaper Al-Araby Al-Jadeed.

The newspaper said Washington and Tehran have made concessions regarding Iran’s nuclear programme and frozen assets.

“Tehran will announce a concession on its nuclear programme in return for Washington announcing the release of part of Iran’s frozen assets,” the sources said, noting that the announcements would be made simultaneously.

Discussions are underway on arrangements for both sides to announce the agreement simultaneously, including initial steps and an interim deal that would pave the way for renewed negotiations.

Separately, Iran said that Washington's response to its demands was "not convincing", insisting that the Strait of Hormuz would reopen only after the US fulfilled seven Iranian conditions.

"The US response to Iran's rights and demands was not convincing," Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei said on X.

"They must respond fully and explicitly to Iran's seven conditions and fulfil them. Only then will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened," he added.

Tehran's reported seven conditions include a ceasefire across the Middle East, the release of Iranian assets frozen abroad and the lifting of sanctions on Iran's oil sector.

The demands also include ending the US naval blockade, paying war reparations, withdrawing US forces and ending threats and interference.

Tensions in the Middle East have remained high since the US and Israel launched attacks against Iran on February 28. Tehran retaliated by targeting Israel and US assets in the region before a ceasefire agreement was reached in April.

Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding on freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz on June 18, but its implementation stalled over disagreements concerning security in the strait.

Mediation efforts

Earlier, Qatar said the United States and Iran were committed to mediation efforts and were reviewing proposals aimed at bridging their differences.

"Both parties remain committed to the negotiation process; as we mentioned, we are facilitating the real-time exchange of proposals between them,” foreign ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari told reporters, according to Reuters and Al-Arabiya.

"We remain hopeful that there is still a chance for a deal to set the environment for future negotiations", he said.

Qatar said that both the United States and Iran remained committed to mediation efforts and were reviewing proposals put forward by mediators. While the Qatari team that travelled to Tehran had since returned to Doha, talks were continuing, Qatar's foreign ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said.

"There are intensive joint regional efforts underway to avoid escalation," he told a news briefing, adding that the "bridging" of gaps "is ongoing"

Three tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy quoted as saying

Three oil tankers struck mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday after entering unauthorised shipping lanes with their navigation and identification systems switched off, the semi-official Tasnim news agency quoted Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy as saying.

The vessels were left burning off the southern coast of the strait, the IRGC Navy said, warning ships against ignoring Iranian regulations and cooperating with the US military to transit unauthorised routes.

Iran-US deal still out of reach despite diplomatic push, Iranian official says

Iran and the United States remain far from a deal to end the war, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday, despite intensified diplomatic efforts to avert a return to major conflict after the US midterm elections.

Overnight, the US carried out "defensive" strikes on Iran's Qeshm island, with a US official saying the strikes targeted surface-to-air missiles used against US assets. Another official said the strikes appeared to be limited and did not signal a resumption of major combat operations.

"Mediators are working hard to narrow gaps between Tehran and Washington," the senior Iranian official said, after Qatari mediators travelled to Tehran on Monday night for talks on a version of a draft US-Iran deal that has been under negotiation for the past eight days.

"Tehran's conditions must be met if the US wants Hormuz reopened," the Iranian official cautioned, referring to the waterway critical for global energy supplies.

The Iranian official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said nuclear talks could only start after Iran's conditions were fulfilled and that Tehran would not accept Washington's "excessive demands".

Tehran would respond forcefully, in the region and beyond, to US strikes, the official added.

Oil prices rose by about $1 on Tuesday, having dropped more than 7% the previous day on hopes diplomacy was progressing.

Additionally, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they downed a US MQ-9 drone and two Lucas drones in the skies near the Strait of Hormuz.

article_html:
The United States approved a draft memorandum of understanding that Qatari mediators presented to Iran a day ago, sources familiar with the matter said on Tuesday.

“The mediation team briefed Saudi Arabia and the UAE on the memorandum, which they also approved,” the sources told Qatari newspaper Al-Araby Al-Jadeed.

The newspaper said Washington and Tehran have made concessions regarding Iran’s nuclear programme and frozen assets.

“Tehran will announce a concession on its nuclear programme in return for Washington announcing the release of part of Iran’s frozen assets,” the sources said, noting that the announcements would be made simultaneously.

Discussions are underway on arrangements for both sides to announce the agreement simultaneously, including initial steps and an interim deal that would pave the way for renewed negotiations.

Separately, Iran said that Washington's response to its demands was "not convincing", insisting that the Strait of Hormuz would reopen only after the US fulfilled seven Iranian conditions.

"The US response to Iran's rights and demands was not convincing," Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei said on X.

"They must respond fully and explicitly to Iran's seven conditions and fulfil them. Only then will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened," he added.

Tehran's reported seven conditions include a ceasefire across the Middle East, the release of Iranian assets frozen abroad and the lifting of sanctions on Iran's oil sector.

The demands also include ending the US naval blockade, paying war reparations, withdrawing US forces and ending threats and interference.

Tensions in the Middle East have remained high since the US and Israel launched attacks against Iran on February 28. Tehran retaliated by targeting Israel and US assets in the region before a ceasefire agreement was reached in April.

Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding on freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz on June 18, but its implementation stalled over disagreements concerning security in the strait.

Mediation efforts

Earlier, Qatar said the United States and Iran were committed to mediation efforts and were reviewing proposals aimed at bridging their differences.

"Both parties remain committed to the negotiation process; as we mentioned, we are facilitating the real-time exchange of proposals between them,” foreign ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari told reporters, according to Reuters and Al-Arabiya.

"We remain hopeful that there is still a chance for a deal to set the environment for future negotiations", he said.

Qatar said that both the United States and Iran remained committed to mediation efforts and were reviewing proposals put forward by mediators. While the Qatari team that travelled to Tehran had since returned to Doha, talks were continuing, Qatar's foreign ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said.

"There are intensive joint regional efforts underway to avoid escalation," he told a news briefing, adding that the "bridging" of gaps "is ongoing"

Three tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy quoted as saying

Three oil tankers struck mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday after entering unauthorised shipping lanes with their navigation and identification systems switched off, the semi-official Tasnim news agency quoted Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy as saying.

The vessels were left burning off the southern coast of the strait, the IRGC Navy said, warning ships against ignoring Iranian regulations and cooperating with the US military to transit unauthorised routes.

Iran-US deal still out of reach despite diplomatic push, Iranian official says

Iran and the United States remain far from a deal to end the war, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday, despite intensified diplomatic efforts to avert a return to major conflict after the US midterm elections.

Overnight, the US carried out "defensive" strikes on Iran's Qeshm island, with a US official saying the strikes targeted surface-to-air missiles used against US assets. Another official said the strikes appeared to be limited and did not signal a resumption of major combat operations.

"Mediators are working hard to narrow gaps between Tehran and Washington," the senior Iranian official said, after Qatari mediators travelled to Tehran on Monday night for talks on a version of a draft US-Iran deal that has been under negotiation for the past eight days.

"Tehran's conditions must be met if the US wants Hormuz reopened," the Iranian official cautioned, referring to the waterway critical for global energy supplies.

The Iranian official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said nuclear talks could only start after Iran's conditions were fulfilled and that Tehran would not accept Washington's "excessive demands".

Tehran would respond forcefully, in the region and beyond, to US strikes, the official added.

Oil prices rose by about $1 on Tuesday, having dropped more than 7% the previous day on hopes diplomacy was progressing.

Additionally, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they downed a US MQ-9 drone and two Lucas drones in the skies near the Strait of Hormuz.

headline: Nathan Fielder was not supposed to appear in Elizabeth Holmes documentary ‘You Can See Everything’
description: Lance Oppenheim reveals how filming Elizabeth Holmes and Billy Evans forced the crew to rethink its approach
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Nathan Fielder was initially expected to produce You Can See Everything, but the documentary took an unexpected direction when he became increasingly involved in filming and eventually joined Lance Oppenheim as co-director.

In an interview on IndieWire’s Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast, Oppenheim explained how the project changed during its first days of production. The documentary follows former Theranos chief executive Elizabeth Holmes and her partner, Billy Evans, in the period before she reported to prison to serve her sentence for defrauding investors.

According to Oppenheim, Fielder initially intended to stay behind the scenes and observe the director’s working methods. However, the original filming approach quickly proved difficult. Oppenheim had planned to use one camera, anamorphic lenses and a small crew, but the confined environment and the couple’s movements made it challenging to capture important moments.

The production soon shifted to a tighter 4:3 aspect ratio and multiple cameras. Two operators used zoom lenses to follow Holmes and Evans, while Oppenheim operated a third camera with a wide-angle lens.

During filming, Holmes and Evans began asking Fielder questions whenever the crew paused to adjust equipment. Their interactions gradually brought him into the documentary itself.

By the second day, Fielder was appearing on camera more frequently. He eventually suggested that he and Oppenheim direct the project together, an idea Oppenheim welcomed.

The filmmakers found that Fielder’s presence allowed them to explore their own confusion about the couple’s behaviour rather than simply observe events from a distance.

Oppenheim said the revised approach enabled the crew to film for extended periods, allowing interactions to unfold without the pressure of traditional interviews.

The director described the finished documentary as a particularly rigorous form of vérité filmmaking, built around observing events as they happened.

headline: Pakistan offers to share energy crisis management experience with Bangladesh
description: Petroleum minister briefs Bangladeshi adviser on efforts to secure fuel supplies amid global challenges
author: APP
article_text:
Pakistan on Tuesday offered to share its experience in managing the global energy crisis with Bangladesh as Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and Bangladesh’s Adviser on Finance Rashid Al Mehmood Titumir discussed fuel supply challenges and the impact of disruptions on international energy markets.

During a meeting, both sides discussed their strategies to manage the unprecedented energy crisis, ensure uninterrupted fuel supplies, and reduce the impact of rising uncertainty in energy markets on their economies, according to a press release.

Malik briefed the Bangladeshi advisor on Pakistan’s efforts to secure fuel supplies amid challenging global circumstances. He also shared details of the government’s initiatives, including targeted fuel subsidies, to provide relief to the public while managing the impact of the crisis.

Titumir shared the steps taken by Bangladesh to ensure fuel security and address emerging challenges, saying the current crisis had brought energy security to the forefront of policymaking.

He stressed the need to make it a central part of national energy strategies, and highlighted the importance of diversifying energy sources and supply routes to strengthen resilience against global disruptions. The Bangladeshi advisor appreciated Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the conflict involving Iran.

He said de-escalation was essential for global economic stability, as the crisis was affecting economies and energy markets worldwide. He also appreciated Pakistan’s efforts to secure LNG cargoes from Qatar through the Strait of Hormuz despite challenging circumstances.

The petroleum minister described the situation as an unprecedented energy crisis. He stressed the importance of preparedness, diversification and regional cooperation in dealing with global energy disruptions.

He expressed Pakistan’s willingness to share its experiences and lessons with Bangladesh to help it manage the energy crisis and strengthen energy security.

Both sides stressed the importance of continued engagement and sharing experiences to address common energy challenges and build greater resilience against future global supply disruptions.

'Closed for debt but open for business in equity'

A day earlier, Titumir proposed a five-point development paradigm for South Asia to deal with disruptive geopolitical challenges, emphasising that legitimacy matters for becoming a welfare state.

In his keynote speech at the annual Sustainable Development Policy Conference, Titumir said regional countries needed to reconstruct the fiscal state, reposition industrial policies and build multilateral cooperation.

He said there was a need to rethink conventional fiscal consolidation, whose purpose should be to preserve the state's capacity to invest in the future, not simply to minimise public expenditure.

Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Dr Musadiq Malik shared those concerns, saying debt-driven growth was unacceptable as servicing was eating half the country's revenues.

"I would propose that we could come up with a South Asian framing of a new development paradigm," with at least five strategic priorities, Titumir said.

He proposed moving from efficiency-driven development to resilience-oriented development, saying recent crises showed that efficiency without resilience creates significant vulnerabilities.

Titumir also proposed repositioning industrial policy as an instrument of structural transformation, saying the challenge was no longer simply to attract investment. "It is to attract investment that builds domestic capabilities, generates employment, transfers technology, and strengthens linkages with the wider economy," he said.

He called for a production network where South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Middle East and North Africa work together across primary, intermediate and finished goods, while remaining mindful of an active industrial policy.

He suggested reconstructing the fiscal state and rethinking development financing, saying the state's capacity to mobilise and allocate resources was becoming a critical determinant of national resilience. Developing countries, he said, needed stronger domestic revenue mobilisation, more efficient spending, modernised public financial management and more sophisticated capital markets.

His fourth proposal placed human capabilities and employment at the centre of economic transformation.

Fifth, he also stressed multilateral cooperation, saying no country, irrespective of economic or military strength, can independently resolve challenges such as climate change, pandemics, financial instability, technological governance, international taxation and maritime security.

Sharing Bangladesh's experience, the finance adviser said: "The foremost lesson that we have learned in Bangladesh, if we are to say it in a single sentence, is that legitimacy matters."

"Legitimacy must originate from the people. So what we are trying to do is come up with a prime ministerial vision of a Bangladesh which is democratic, which is humane, and which has a welfare state," he said.

headline: PHC sends petitions challenging detentions of Afridi, others to CJ to form larger bench
description: Gohar expresses gratitude at court's decision, says 'political tension should not escalate further'
author: Yasir Ali
article_text:
The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Tuesday said a larger bench should be constituted to hear the petitions regarding the whereabouts of Sohail Afridi, non-functional Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) chief minister, Provincial Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, and MNA Junaid Akbar, among others, saying that the case was being sent to the chief justice.

Justice Syed Arshad Ali and Justice Muhammad Faheem Wali heard the cases and said they were being sent to the CJ, who should constitute a larger bench. Advocate General Sanaullah also stated, "It is our request too that a larger bench be constituted."

On October 13, Afridi's brother moved the PHC seeking the non-functional CM's immediate recovery, arguing that his alleged abduction and continued detention violated his fundamental rights and demanding an independent judicial inquiry into his disappearance. The petition was filed amid uncertainty over Afridi’s whereabouts following the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in K-P on October 11, which brought the PTI-led provincial government to an end and transferred its powers to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi.

During Tuesday's hearing, the petitioners' counsel Advocate Bashir Khan Wazir said during the hearing that Afridi and Swati had been "missing for several days," adding that the K-P governor and advisers had "confirmed that the chief minister, the speaker, and Junaid Akbar are in protective custody."

Wazir stated that the provincial assembly had "passed an immunity bill regarding the speaker and members of the assembly," adding that "the chief minister, speaker, and other members cannot be arrested."

Justice Ali also noted, "This is the province's chief minister and speaker; these are not ordinary personalities," adding that this was not a MPO-3 case, referring to Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance. "This is an important case, the province's chief minister is missing," he said.

Advocate General Sanaullah requested time to submit the report, saying that it had been sought from the police, law enforcement agencies, and the Home Department. He also noted that there were "more than 200 cases of MPO-3."

Justice Ali however, said that the advocate general had been given 10 days by the court. "You are not complying with the court's orders," he said. Petitioners' counsel Yasir Khattak argued that "the court issues order, they do not comply with them," adding that the court had ordered the de-sealing of the house of the deputy speaker of the provincial assembly, which had still not been implemented by authorities. "They are committing contempt of court," he said

Meanwhile, K-P Bar Council member Advocate Farooq Ahmed Khattak stated that if the officials had been "picked up under MPO-3, tell the court."

Barrister Gohar expresses gratitude for court's decision

Meanwhile, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, expressed gratitude that the PHC referred the matter to the chief justice. Speaking to media outside the PHC, Barrister Gohar stated, "It is a strange logic; the chief minister and speaker are missing."

Expressing gratitude at the court's decision, he noted that "decisions should be such that they are equal for everyone." The PTI chairman also stated that "political tension should not escalate further," saying political matters "should be resolved by sitting down and finding a solution."

Gohar reiterated PTI's demand for a meeting with founder Imran Khan, as well as his medical treatment, arguing that "even the courts' decision was not accepted."

"The public is suffering because of this," he said, calling for the "series of political revenge" to end. The chairman also stated that MNA's, MPA's, and Imran's sisters should be "released immediately."

Imran's sisters were detained in September under Section 3 of the MPO as PTI prepared for a planned protest march towards Islamabad. Aleema was detained on September 20, while Uzma and Noreen were taken into custody on September 21. Their initial detention orders were issued for 30 days. The orders were later extended another 30 days.

Barrister Gohar also noted that lawyer Salman Safdar had met Imran a day earlier, saying that "had this happened earlier, there would not have been so much trouble."

article_html:
PESHAWAR:

The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Tuesday said a larger bench should be constituted to hear the petitions regarding the whereabouts of Sohail Afridi, non-functional Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) chief minister, Provincial Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, and MNA Junaid Akbar, among others, saying that the case was being sent to the chief justice.

Justice Syed Arshad Ali and Justice Muhammad Faheem Wali heard the cases and said they were being sent to the CJ, who should constitute a larger bench. Advocate General Sanaullah also stated, "It is our request too that a larger bench be constituted."

On October 13, Afridi's brother moved the PHC seeking the non-functional CM's immediate recovery, arguing that his alleged abduction and continued detention violated his fundamental rights and demanding an independent judicial inquiry into his disappearance. The petition was filed amid uncertainty over Afridi’s whereabouts following the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in K-P on October 11, which brought the PTI-led provincial government to an end and transferred its powers to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi.

Read: PHC seeks replies from governor, speaker against governor’s rule

During Tuesday's hearing, the petitioners' counsel Advocate Bashir Khan Wazir said during the hearing that Afridi and Swati had been "missing for several days," adding that the K-P governor and advisers had "confirmed that the chief minister, the speaker, and Junaid Akbar are in protective custody."

Wazir stated that the provincial assembly had "passed an immunity bill regarding the speaker and members of the assembly," adding that "the chief minister, speaker, and other members cannot be arrested."

Justice Ali also noted, "This is the province's chief minister and speaker; these are not ordinary personalities," adding that this was not a MPO-3 case, referring to Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance. "This is an important case, the province's chief minister is missing," he said.

Advocate General Sanaullah requested time to submit the report, saying that it had been sought from the police, law enforcement agencies, and the Home Department. He also noted that there were "more than 200 cases of MPO-3."

Justice Ali however, said that the advocate general had been given 10 days by the court. "You are not complying with the court's orders," he said. Petitioners' counsel Yasir Khattak argued that "the court issues order, they do not comply with them," adding that the court had ordered the de-sealing of the house of the deputy speaker of the provincial assembly, which had still not been implemented by authorities. "They are committing contempt of court," he said

Meanwhile, K-P Bar Council member Advocate Farooq Ahmed Khattak stated that if the officials had been "picked up under MPO-3, tell the court."

Barrister Gohar expresses gratitude for court's decision

Meanwhile, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, expressed gratitude that the PHC referred the matter to the chief justice. Speaking to media outside the PHC, Barrister Gohar stated, "It is a strange logic; the chief minister and speaker are missing."

Expressing gratitude at the court's decision, he noted that "decisions should be such that they are equal for everyone." The PTI chairman also stated that "political tension should not escalate further," saying political matters "should be resolved by sitting down and finding a solution."

Gohar reiterated PTI's demand for a meeting with founder Imran Khan, as well as his medical treatment, arguing that "even the courts' decision was not accepted."

"The public is suffering because of this," he said, calling for the "series of political revenge" to end. The chairman also stated that MNA's, MPA's, and Imran's sisters should be "released immediately."

Read More: K-P governor's rule to end in six months, emergency to continue until peace restored: Tariq Fazal

Imran's sisters were detained in September under Section 3 of the MPO as PTI prepared for a planned protest march towards Islamabad. Aleema was detained on September 20, while Uzma and Noreen were taken into custody on September 21. Their initial detention orders were issued for 30 days. The orders were later extended another 30 days.

Barrister Gohar also noted that lawyer Salman Safdar had met Imran a day earlier, saying that "had this happened earlier, there would not have been so much trouble."

Safdar, who serves as a lead counsel in several cases involving Imran and his wife Bushra, later published a brief post on X on Monday night, stating that the meeting facilitated by the jail administration started at around 4:30pm and continued for 40 minutes. According to Safdar, he was permitted to meet the PTI founder and his wife despite repeated requests and applications, respectively, after seven and eleven months.

Reiterating the call for talks, Barrister Gohar stated that an offer was "present on the table," and that "talks should be held with seriousness and good faith."

headline: Paris Jackson seeks $600m trust fund from Michael Jackson's estate
description: Paris Jackson has asked court to fund her father's family trust, claiming it remains unfunded 17 years after his death
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Paris Jackson has petitioned a Los Angeles probate court to order a $600 million distribution from her late father Michael Jackson's estate to the Michael Jackson Family Trust, arguing that the fund remains unfunded more than 17 years after his death.

According to legal documents obtained by TheWrap, Paris claims her father intended for his children, including brothers Prince and Bigi Jackson, to receive income from the trust when they turned 21.

However, she argues that all three siblings have passed that milestone without receiving the intended distributions.

"More than 17 years after his passing, Michael Jackson's family trust remains unfunded," the filing states. It also claims that the estate's executors have yet to present the court with a plan for funding the trust.

Paris's legal team argues that the estate has accumulated substantial cash through business deals and asset sales, including its interest in EMI Music Publishing, Neverland Ranch and an agreement with Sony involving the singer's music and intellectual property.

"Indeed, Paris is informed that, even when potential liabilities are taken into account, the Estate holds approximately $600 million in distributable cash, not to mention any cash that may be held at the entity level," the filing states.

The petition also raises concerns about the timing of future distributions, noting that Michael Jackson intended for his children to begin receiving trust principal when they turned 30. Prince will reach that age in four months, while Paris turns 29 in April and Bigi turns 25 in February.

In response, the Michael Jackson Estate told People that the trusts could not be fully funded until outstanding legal matters were resolved, including a dispute with the Internal Revenue Service over $700 million in taxes and penalties.

The estate said the tax dispute had been significantly reduced but remained unresolved. It also rejected claims that beneficiaries' payments were being withheld or reduced as a "complete fabrication", adding: "None of his children receive a distribution until they are in their 30s."

headline: Tenerife striker De Miguel dies after collision
description: Jesus de Miguel succumbs to injuries suffered in a horrific on-field clash with Andorra goalkeeper
author: AFP .
article_text: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died on Tuesday as a result of injuries he suffered in a sickening collision with FC Andorra's goalkeeper in a Spanish second division match. "Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe this is real, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death, at 8:00 am (7am GMT), of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," his club Tenerife said in a statement. "No words can ease the pain, nothing can lessen this great feeling of sadness. Our thoughts are with the family, his close friends and Tenerife fans, who today are grieving over this terrible news." De Miguel, 30, was fouled in the middle of the pitch by Equatorial Guinea international goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who had raced out of his goal to try and clear the ball. The incident happened towards the end of the match at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium, with the teams level at 2-2. Owono was sent off and the match was subsequently abandoned. Spanish media said that De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest and was resuscitated. The player was taken to hospital and placed in intensive care, with Tenerife later saying that De Miguel's condition had "worsened neurologically", before his death. "I am so deeply sorry. Rest in peace, Jesus," former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique, Andorra's majority shareholder, wrote on social media. Andorra also sent their "most sincere condolences" to De Miguel's family, team-mates and Tenerife. Real Madrid, Barcelona, Atletico Madrid and other clubs in Spain also sent messages of condolence, as well as the Spanish football federation (RFEF). "Shattered by this sad news, the Royal Spanish Football Federation wishes to express our deepest sorrow at his passing today," wrote the federation in a statement. The RFEF postponed Tuesday's matches in the Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina, "as a gesture of respect and solidarity". Real Madrid held a minute of silence before their training session on Tuesday. "Immense sadness, there are no words," Madrid's French forward Kylian Mbappe wrote on Instagram. La Liga side Espanyol also delayed the presentation of their new coach Eder Sarabia to Wednesday. Top flight chief Javier Tebas and Spanish sports minister Milagros Tolon also posted messages of condolence. "Today we all share the terrible pain of an irreparable loss," wrote Tebas on X. "We share in your grief," wrote Tolon, offering her "deepest condolences to (De Miguel's) family and loved ones", as well as Tenerife, the players and staff. De Miguel had been at Tenerife for just over a season, having joined in the summer of 2025 from Castellon. The striker helped the team gain promotion to the second division. The forward began his career with Leganes at youth level in the Madrid suburbs, playing for a string of teams, including Unionistas de Salamanca, before signing for Castellon in 2023.

headline: Zohran Mamdani trolls JD Vance’s New York City boasts with viral subway meme
description: Mamdani shared the footage without adding an explanation, leaving viewers to interpret the apparent joke
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has responded to Vice President JD Vance’s claims about the Trump administration’s achievements in New York with a brief video that has attracted widespread attention online.

Vance shared a post on X on Monday, November 2, listing what he described as the administration’s accomplishments for the city and state.

These included safer communities, tax cuts for working families and “historic investments” in New York. He ended the post by writing, “We got your back, New York!”

However, the claims faced scrutiny after an X Community Note challenged several figures, arguing that some investments were nationwide pledges rather than New York-specific results.

It also disputed the attribution of a reported 48% drop in murders, linking the figure to New York’s state-run GIVE programme.

Mamdani then responded with a 9-second video featuring online prankster Olly Bee, who describes himself as the “worlds hardest worker”.

Originally posted by Bee in December 2025, the clip shows him wearing a high-visibility vest and appearing to help a subway train stop, open its doors, welcome passengers, close the doors and continue its journey.

Mamdani shared the footage without adding an explanation, leaving viewers to interpret the apparent joke as a dig at Vance’s claims.

The video quickly gained traction, with one Reddit user describing the exchange as a “brutal” response to the vice president.

Bee also welcomed the unexpected attention, writing in an Instagram Story, “HOLY SH*T @zohrankmamdani LETS COLLAB PLEASE”.

headline: Dar reaffirms govt's commitment to public relief in meeting with JI delegation
description: Parties discuss relief measures for common man, with specific focus on easing economic burden on low-income citizens
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday reaffirmed the government's commitment to providing relief to the public amid global economic challenges during a meeting with a Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) delegation led by Liaquat Baloch to discuss petroleum prices and measures to ease the financial burden on low-income citizens.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday met with a delegation of the Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) to discuss petroleum prices in the country, with both sides agreeing to "continue their consultations over the coming days to formulate a way forward on energy pricing and public relief," the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement.

"Dar met with the JI delegation led by Liaquat Baloch, holding candid discussions on practical measures to provide relief to the common man, with a specific focus on easing the economic burden on low-income citizens," said the Foreign Office in a post on X.

The meeting came after the government and JI, on October 27, agreed to form a six-member committee to finalise recommendations on expanding the existing petrol relief scheme and preparing proposals for a phased reduction in the petroleum levy. Under the agreement, three members each from the government and JI would examine measures to broaden the scope of the ongoing PM fuel relief scheme to ensure that the maximum number of deserving people benefit from it.

Agreeing to continue consultations, Dar also "reiterated the government’s commitment to prioritising public welfare and facilitating ordinary citizens amidst global economic challenges."

He also "emphasised that sustained cross-party dialogue remains key to addressing national economic challenges effectively."

The Foreign Office stated that the meeting was attended by the Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Inter-Provincial Coordination Rana Sanaullah, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Tariq Bajwa, along with the finance secretary and the Special secretary for petroleum.

Background

JI’s campaign against the petroleum levy intensified in August, when the party organised demonstrations and sit-ins across the country against rising fuel prices, inflation and what it described as an additional tax burden on consumers. On August 16, JI workers staged sit-ins outside governors’ houses in the provincial capitals, demanding the withdrawal of the levy and a reduction in petrol prices.

The party subsequently expanded its protests to other cities, including Karachi, where it established additional protest camps across Sindh. JI maintained that the government should abolish the levy rather than offer limited reductions in fuel prices.

On September 3, the government and JI agreed to establish technical committees to examine proposals for reducing the petroleum levy and fuel prices. During the first round of negotiations on September 7, the party submitted six proposals to the government, while insisting that its protests would continue until meaningful relief was provided.

However, the negotiations failed to resolve the dispute. On September 12, JI chief announced a long march towards Islamabad for September 20, warning that the party would intensify its campaign if the government did not abolish the levy.

The march began on September 20, with participants travelling from Karachi by train. The caravan moved through Sukkur towards Multan, where Naeem addressed supporters. The march was subsequently suspended after PM Shehbaz telephoned the JI chief and requested that the party postpone its protest to allow further negotiations.

JI agreed to give the government an opportunity for talks but maintained that it had not abandoned its demand. The party’s position was that negotiations and protests could continue simultaneously, with any agreement required to address the complete abolition of the levy.

article_html:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday reaffirmed the government's commitment to providing relief to the public amid global economic challenges during a meeting with a Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) delegation led by Liaquat Baloch to discuss petroleum prices and measures to ease the financial burden on low-income citizens.

 

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday met with a delegation of the Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) to discuss petroleum prices in the country, with both sides agreeing to "continue their consultations over the coming days to formulate a way forward on energy pricing and public relief," the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement.

"Dar met with the JI delegation led by Liaquat Baloch, holding candid discussions on practical measures to provide relief to the common man, with a specific focus on easing the economic burden on low-income citizens," said the Foreign Office in a post on X.

The meeting came after the government and JI, on October 27, agreed to form a six-member committee to finalise recommendations on expanding the existing petrol relief scheme and preparing proposals for a phased reduction in the petroleum levy. Under the agreement, three members each from the government and JI would examine measures to broaden the scope of the ongoing PM fuel relief scheme to ensure that the maximum number of deserving people benefit from it.

Read: Govt stands firm on petroleum levy

Agreeing to continue consultations, Dar also "reiterated the government’s commitment to prioritising public welfare and facilitating ordinary citizens amidst global economic challenges."

He also "emphasised that sustained cross-party dialogue remains key to addressing national economic challenges effectively."

The Foreign Office stated that the meeting was attended by the Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Inter-Provincial Coordination Rana Sanaullah, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Tariq Bajwa, along with the finance secretary and the Special secretary for petroleum.

Background

JI’s campaign against the petroleum levy intensified in August, when the party organised demonstrations and sit-ins across the country against rising fuel prices, inflation and what it described as an additional tax burden on consumers. On August 16, JI workers staged sit-ins outside governors’ houses in the provincial capitals, demanding the withdrawal of the levy and a reduction in petrol prices.

The party subsequently expanded its protests to other cities, including Karachi, where it established additional protest camps across Sindh. JI maintained that the government should abolish the levy rather than offer limited reductions in fuel prices.

On September 3, the government and JI agreed to establish technical committees to examine proposals for reducing the petroleum levy and fuel prices. During the first round of negotiations on September 7, the party submitted six proposals to the government, while insisting that its protests would continue until meaningful relief was provided.

However, the negotiations failed to resolve the dispute. On September 12, JI chief announced a long march towards Islamabad for September 20, warning that the party would intensify its campaign if the government did not abolish the levy.

Read More: JI launches third phase of protest campaign against petroleum levy

The march began on September 20, with participants travelling from Karachi by train. The caravan moved through Sukkur towards Multan, where Naeem addressed supporters. The march was subsequently suspended after PM Shehbaz telephoned the JI chief and requested that the party postpone its protest to allow further negotiations.

JI agreed to give the government an opportunity for talks but maintained that it had not abandoned its demand. The party’s position was that negotiations and protests could continue simultaneously, with any agreement required to address the complete abolition of the levy.

The JI chief then gave the government 10 days to abolish the petroleum levy and provide meaningful relief to the inflation-hit public, warning that his party would resume its long march towards Islamabad in mid-November if its demands were not met.

headline: US intelligence sharing has fractured under Trump, officials say
description: Troubles came during Tulsi Gabbard's tenure as director of national intelligence, amid tensions with CIA
author: Reuters
article_text:
US intelligence sharing on Iran and other global threats with Congress and across the federal government has slowed and, in some cases, temporarily stopped during President Donald Trump's second term, according to eight current and former officials and people briefed on the matter.

Former officials and outside experts said the disruptions risk leaving policymakers with an incomplete picture of threats facing the country, echoing intelligence failures exposed after the September 11, 2001, al Qaeda attacks. The slowdown comes as the administration weighs whether to resume strikes on Iran after the midterm elections on Tuesday.

The problems emerged during Tulsi Gabbard's tenure as director of national intelligence, amid deep tensions between her office and the CIA. While those tensions have subsided since her resignation in June, problems stemming from the clash persist, according to two US officials familiar with the matter.

The CIA has stopped co-authoring assessments with the National Intelligence Council (NIC), an analytical group within the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), the officials said, reducing the number of reports that pull together the intelligence community's views for decision-makers on subjects including Iran.

Lawmakers and their staffs also briefly stopped receiving intelligence reports from Gabbard's office in the days after the US military intervention in Iran in June 2025 and again after the capture of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in January 2026, according to two people familiar with the matter. Gabbard's team had accused lawmakers of leaking to the press.

The disruption in intelligence sharing has not been previously reported.

CIA spokesperson Liz Lyons said the CIA "participates fully" in the process of providing intelligence assessments through the Presidential Daily Brief, which is led by ODNI, and through the NIC.

Now, some former officials are working on a bipartisan basis at Stanford University's Hoover Institution to draw up plans to rebuild the intelligence community in the next administration, four former US officials said.

“All of these things are adding up in a really complex world where policymakers need to have a more sophisticated, nuanced, and integrated view of the world, and they are getting less,” said Beth Sanner, a former deputy director of national intelligence during Trump's first term.

Turf wars and reduced cooperation

The problems inside the intelligence community started last year amid significant cuts to national security agencies, including the ODNI and the CIA, as Trump moved to remove or sideline officials he viewed as disloyal.

Some analysts who remain at the intelligence agencies are now careful not to write assessments at odds with White House’s views for fear of political retaliation, two former officials and a current US official said. The officials did not say which topics the analysts were avoiding.

“Analysts still do the work, but this White House has made them irrelevant because the president treats unwelcome information as disloyalty,” said Julia Curlee, a former CIA analyst who said she was fired from the Trump National Security Council last year for being transgender.

The White House did not respond to a request for comment.

The situation was worsened by what officials described as one of the biggest turf wars in three decades between two of the most important agencies: the CIA and the ODNI, which was formed in the aftermath of the September 11 attacks.

Reuters earlier detailed the dispute between the agencies.

The infighting between the agencies — triggered when Gabbard's office revoked the security clearances of current and former intelligence officials a year ago — reached the point where White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles had to intervene several times to defuse tensions, three former officials said.

The National Intelligence Council, which for decades has been a key resource for officials and lawmakers making foreign policy decisions, lost its main author when the CIA stopped writing into the assessments last year.

The assessments are meant to consolidate the views of the nation’s 18 intelligence agencies, and the council relied heavily on the CIA for analysis on topics like Iran and Russia.

While the CIA continued sharing intelligence with the NIC and working with it on some reports, its analysts focused on their own assessments.

Since the move, the intelligence council, which was also hit by staff cuts, has slowed production of its assessments, two people familiar with the matter said. None have focused on the war in Iran, five current and former officials said.

In response to a request for comment, an ODNI official said the group has maintained assessment levels close to "historic trendlines."

"While Tulsi did not utilise the NIC, DNI Clayton has proven to be a good steward of the IC and recognises the value of the NIC," said a US official, referring to Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton.

New barriers

Some former intelligence officials worry that new barriers are appearing between agencies.

"The problem is that by taking actions which have the effect of hollowing out institutions where there's actual intelligence community coordination on things, you're creating little lily pads, and then everybody can pick their own lily pad to listen to,” said Morgan Muir, the former deputy director of national intelligence in the Biden administration who also briefed President George W. Bush.

Gabbard's office also stopped briefing Congress on election threats in 2025, according to two people familiar with the matter and a former US official.

Clayton, who became director of national intelligence in August, has resumed congressional briefings on election threats, officials said.

"Director Clayton remains committed to ensuring that ODNI and the intelligence community have the resources they need to continue informing key US government decision-makers and keeping Americans safe," ODNI said in a statement to Reuters.

In another clash between agencies, the FBI late last year stopped sharing some intelligence with the National Counterterrorism Centre for several weeks after the centre's then-head, Joe Kent, and his staff tried to investigate the shooting of Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk, two former officials said.

FBI leaders told Kent they believed NCTC was overstepping its authority.

The FBI did not respond to a request for comment.

article_html:
US intelligence sharing on Iran and other global threats with Congress and across the federal government has slowed and, in some cases, temporarily stopped during President Donald Trump's second term, according to eight current and former officials and people briefed on the matter.

Former officials and outside experts said the disruptions risk leaving policymakers with an incomplete picture of threats facing the country, echoing intelligence failures exposed after the September 11, 2001, al Qaeda attacks. The slowdown comes as the administration weighs whether to resume strikes on Iran after the midterm elections on Tuesday.

The problems emerged during Tulsi Gabbard's tenure as director of national intelligence, amid deep tensions between her office and the CIA. While those tensions have subsided since her resignation in June, problems stemming from the clash persist, according to two US officials familiar with the matter.

The CIA has stopped co-authoring assessments with the National Intelligence Council (NIC), an analytical group within the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), the officials said, reducing the number of reports that pull together the intelligence community's views for decision-makers on subjects including Iran.

Lawmakers and their staffs also briefly stopped receiving intelligence reports from Gabbard's office in the days after the US military intervention in Iran in June 2025 and again after the capture of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in January 2026, according to two people familiar with the matter. Gabbard's team had accused lawmakers of leaking to the press.

Read: Iranian strikes caused billions in damage to US intelligence sites: report

The disruption in intelligence sharing has not been previously reported.

CIA spokesperson Liz Lyons said the CIA "participates fully" in the process of providing intelligence assessments through the Presidential Daily Brief, which is led by ODNI, and through the NIC.

Now, some former officials are working on a bipartisan basis at Stanford University's Hoover Institution to draw up plans to rebuild the intelligence community in the next administration, four former US officials said.

“All of these things are adding up in a really complex world where policymakers need to have a more sophisticated, nuanced, and integrated view of the world, and they are getting less,” said Beth Sanner, a former deputy director of national intelligence during Trump's first term.

Turf wars and reduced cooperation

The problems inside the intelligence community started last year amid significant cuts to national security agencies, including the ODNI and the CIA, as Trump moved to remove or sideline officials he viewed as disloyal.

Some analysts who remain at the intelligence agencies are now careful not to write assessments at odds with White House’s views for fear of political retaliation, two former officials and a current US official said. The officials did not say which topics the analysts were avoiding.

“Analysts still do the work, but this White House has made them irrelevant because the president treats unwelcome information as disloyalty,” said Julia Curlee, a former CIA analyst who said she was fired from the Trump National Security Council last year for being transgender.

The White House did not respond to a request for comment.

The situation was worsened by what officials described as one of the biggest turf wars in three decades between two of the most important agencies: the CIA and the ODNI, which was formed in the aftermath of the September 11 attacks.

Read more: Trump administration conducting mass firings at top US intelligence agency: CNN

Reuters earlier detailed the dispute between the agencies.

The infighting between the agencies — triggered when Gabbard's office revoked the security clearances of current and former intelligence officials a year ago — reached the point where White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles had to intervene several times to defuse tensions, three former officials said.

The National Intelligence Council, which for decades has been a key resource for officials and lawmakers making foreign policy decisions, lost its main author when the CIA stopped writing into the assessments last year.

The assessments are meant to consolidate the views of the nation’s 18 intelligence agencies, and the council relied heavily on the CIA for analysis on topics like Iran and Russia.

While the CIA continued sharing intelligence with the NIC and working with it on some reports, its analysts focused on their own assessments.

Since the move, the intelligence council, which was also hit by staff cuts, has slowed production of its assessments, two people familiar with the matter said. None have focused on the war in Iran, five current and former officials said.

In response to a request for comment, an ODNI official said the group has maintained assessment levels close to "historic trendlines."

"While Tulsi did not utilise the NIC, DNI Clayton has proven to be a good steward of the IC and recognises the value of the NIC," said a US official, referring to Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton.

New barriers

Some former intelligence officials worry that new barriers are appearing between agencies.

"The problem is that by taking actions which have the effect of hollowing out institutions where there's actual intelligence community coordination on things, you're creating little lily pads, and then everybody can pick their own lily pad to listen to,” said Morgan Muir, the former deputy director of national intelligence in the Biden administration who also briefed President George W. Bush.

Gabbard's office also stopped briefing Congress on election threats in 2025, according to two people familiar with the matter and a former US official.

Clayton, who became director of national intelligence in August, has resumed congressional briefings on election threats, officials said.

Also read: US intelligence warns Israel could undermine Iran peace deal: report

"Director Clayton remains committed to ensuring that ODNI and the intelligence community have the resources they need to continue informing key US government decision-makers and keeping Americans safe," ODNI said in a statement to Reuters.

In another clash between agencies, the FBI late last year stopped sharing some intelligence with the National Counterterrorism Centre for several weeks after the centre's then-head, Joe Kent, and his staff tried to investigate the shooting of Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk, two former officials said.

FBI leaders told Kent they believed NCTC was overstepping its authority.

The FBI did not respond to a request for comment.

headline: Taylor Swift opens up about why she hesitated to write a song for 'Toy Story 5'
description: Swift reveals why she was concerned about taking the 'Toy Story 5' song opportunity from another artist
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Taylor Swift has revealed that she initially worried about taking the opportunity to write an original song for Pixar’s upcoming film, Toy Story 5, from another artist.

The 36-year-old singer discussed the experience during a question-and-answer session with director Andrew Stanton following a special screening on Sunday, November 1.

According to Billboard, the conversation explored how Swift came to create “I Knew It, I Knew You” for the animated film.

Stanton explained that Swift was his preferred choice for the project as he wanted to take the soundtrack in a different direction.

Randy Newman, who has composed music for the franchise since the original 1995 film, was not returning for the same role.

“Nothing else made sense,” Stanton said.

Swift was initially unavailable, leading Stanton to believe the film might not have an original end-credits song. However, the singer continued contacting the director to check whether the opportunity was still available or had been offered to someone else.

She explained that she would have understood if the filmmakers had moved forward without her, given the months it took her to respond.

“I don’t want to kick somebody off of this project that you reached out to after [me],” she added. “I understand, but I’m not in the business of doing that.”

Swift eventually wrote “I Knew It, I Knew You”, which went on to reach No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and break multiple records.

The track has also attracted Oscar buzz, adding to anticipation surrounding its appearance in Toy Story 5.

A producer on the Pixar film also reportedly sent Swift a personal letter asking her to contribute an original song.

headline: Johnny Depp reveals one condition for returning to ‘Pirates of the Caribbean 6’
description: Johnny Depp says he trusts longtime friend and producer Jerry Bruckheimer with the franchise’s future
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Johnny Depp has opened up about the possibility of reprising his iconic role as Captain Jack Sparrow in Pirates of the Caribbean 6, revealing that he would consider returning for one important reason: giving the franchise a satisfying conclusion.

Speaking to Variety during the promotional tour for his upcoming film Ebenezer, Depp addressed speculation surrounding his potential involvement in the next instalment. Although he stopped short of confirming his return, the actor expressed a willingness to work with longtime friend and producer Jerry Bruckheimer.

“If things are exactly where they need to be with regard to how they are going to top off the ‘Pirates’ franchise… the only involvement I really want to have, truly, is just to send them off on a better note,” Depp said.

He also reaffirmed his trust in Bruckheimer, adding that he would work with the producer again regardless of the project. Their longstanding friendship, he explained, remains an important factor in his willingness to consider returning.

Bruckheimer previously expressed optimism about Depp reprising the role. In 2025, the producer told Entertainment Weekly that the actor could be interested if he liked the screenplay. At the time, the script was still being developed, with the creative team searching for the right story.

Depp played Jack Sparrow across five films released between 2003 and 2017. The franchise has generated approximately $4.5 billion worldwide, making it one of Disney’s most commercially successful film series.

Plans for a sixth film have been in development for years. Screenwriter Jeff Nathanson, who worked on Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales, was previously attached to the project. Bruckheimer has also publicly voiced support for Depp’s involvement.

However, no official casting confirmation or production announcement has been made regarding Depp’s return.

headline: ‘Primetime’ digital release: Where to stream Robert Pattinson’s new thriller
description: The film explores a controversial television sting operation inspired by real events from 2006
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
A24’s thriller Primetime, starring Robert Pattinson as former television presenter Chris Hansen, is now available to watch at home following its theatrical release.

The film arrives on premium video on demand platforms on November 3, allowing viewers to rent or purchase it digitally. Available retailers include Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV and Fandango at Home.

On Apple TV, Primetime is listed for $19.99 to rent and $24.99 to purchase. Prices and availability may vary across platforms and regions.

The digital release comes a little over a month after the film premiered in US cinemas on September 25. It debuted at the Venice International Film Festival on September 5 before its theatrical rollout.

Directed by Lance Oppenheim, Primetime draws inspiration from events surrounding a 2006 television sting operation. The story follows Hansen as he pursues a career defining television moment, only for a high stakes operation to take a devastating turn. A24 describes the film as an exploration of performative justice.

Pattinson leads an ensemble cast that includes Merritt Wever, Skyler Gisondo, Matthew Maher, Bokeem Woodbine, Anna Faris, Alex Winter and Phoebe Bridgers. The screenplay was written by Ajon Singh and adapted from Luke Dittrich’s 2007 Esquire article, “Tonight on Dateline This Man Will Die.”

The film marks Oppenheim’s narrative feature directorial debut. His other work includes the documentary You Can See Everything, which he co directed.

Although Primetime is now available for digital purchase and rental, a subscription streaming release date has not been announced. A potential arrival on HBO Max has been speculated about based on A24’s distribution arrangements, but no official date has been confirmed.
